# Sync Develop — D-family Capability Register

_Program of record for **Sync Develop — Asset Investment & Project Delivery Intelligence**, created 2026-08-27. Direction from the product owner: **build the Sync Develop specification with 100% of its functions and capabilities — control the build so nothing is missed.** This register enumerates every atomic item of the specification (`docs/sync-develop/research/2026-08-27-sync-develop-spec.md`) with a stable ID. An item may only be marked ✅ when the capability demonstrably exists as working code a customer can reach (surface → caller → RPC → persisted → customer-visible), with evidence a reachability gate would accept — not documentation, not schema-only, not demo-seed-only. Status legend: ✅ exists and reachable · 🟡 partial foundation (cited, with the gap named) · ❌ absent. All ❌/🟡 items are open build obligations._

_This file is a separate register from `docs/enterprise-readiness/capability-register.md` (the EOS register, which is contested and append-only). Same discipline applies here: rows are append-and-accept; a status may regress only as an honest, deliberate downgrade explained in the commit that makes it. Companion documents: [overlap-map.md](overlap-map.md) (what already exists and every canonical-home ruling — read it before building ANY row) and [build-plan.md](build-plan.md) (the controlled sequence)._

## Standing constraints (register-visible, binding on every row)

1. **Provenance.** `GateRequirement.source_authority` (LAW → REGULATION → CORPORATE_STANDARD → PROJECT_FRAMEWORK → CONTRACT → INDUSTRY_GUIDANCE → BEST_PRACTICE → AI_SUGGESTION) and `Evidence.provenance` (MEASURED … AI_INFERENCE) are enforced tiers, not labels. Public-Suncor-derived ADEM detail enters only as INDUSTRY_GUIDANCE/INFERRED — never as an authoritative corporate requirement. An AI inference never silently becomes verified evidence; tier promotion is an authorized-human act rejected otherwise at the persistence boundary. We do not market as "we digitized ADEM."
2. **Deterministic boundary (spec §70).** The LLM never determines: **gate passed · risk accepted · regulation satisfied · safety barrier adequate · project sanctioned · equipment safe to start · contract legally compliant.** Rules engines, validated calculations, and authorized humans only — enforced the way this repository already enforces them (BEFORE-triggers raising `check_violation`, SECURITY DEFINER RPCs checking authority, restrictive RLS). The LLM explains, detects, prepares. Every new D-family object ships with its prohibition enforcement on day one.
3. **No fabricated numbers.** Every calculation (§45–§55) refuses on insufficient input and carries its basis/sample count. A gate readiness of 97% is BLOCKED by one failed mandatory item. No baseline → no CPI. No approved benefit baseline → no Value Realization percentage.
4. **Reachable means done.** ✅ requires the full chain a customer can walk. Schema-only, demo-seed-only, and zero-caller RPCs are 🟡 by definition — this repository's own demotion history (74 rows, 2026-08-26) is the reason this rule exists. **ENFORCED since 2026-08-28, not merely stated.** `src/test/capability-reachability.test.ts` now resolves this register's evidence to code and fails the build on any ✅ row citing a symbol with no non-test caller chain, and `scripts/register-baseline.mjs` ratchets it per row so a demotion cannot happen silently. Its first pass demoted seven rows (D2.04, D3.02, D3.03, D3.14, D3.19, D3.24, D3.35) — five of which had already NAMED the gap in their own evidence and kept the ✅ anyway. Between 2026-08-27 and that date this register carried the rule with none of the machinery, which is the only way that could happen.
5. **Extend, never parallel-track.** Every row names its canonical home in [overlap-map.md](overlap-map.md). One asset hierarchy, one evidence model, one decision store, one assumption family, one constraint model, one learning store, one audit ledger (AGENTS.md invariants 1–3, 8).

**Current tally: ✅ 131 · 🟡 72 · ❌ 31 (234 items).** The tally is derived, never hand-typed — recount the glyphs before trusting it. Both the tally and every row's status are CI-checked (`npm run register:check`, `src/test/capability-register.test.ts`).

(2) Two guards were written on `current_user in ('authenticated','anon')` INSIDE `security definer` functions, where `current_user` is always the owner: one was a provably dead disjunct dressed as a wall, and the other meant `gate_review_sod_position` and `gate_requirement_evidence` skipped their organization check for every caller with no org claim — a service-key call could read any tenant's gate evidence by case id. `session_user = 'authenticator'` is the discriminator (verified live: a definer function reports `current_user=postgres session_user=authenticator` over PostgREST for anon, authenticated and the service key alike); both now return `forbidden`. Adoption supersedes PER SCOPE (:adopt re-create) so a site delegation cannot retire the org-wide ladder, and a covering node scope is SELECTED over the org-wide row with its ceiling binding (permit side, not only refusal). HONEST BOUNDARY on the tree dimension: enforcement matches `authority_limits.organization_id = the acting row's organization` BEFORE the node predicate, so org_node_id discriminates only AMONG ladders stored at the same organization row — it refines and refuses there, but it cannot ROUTE authority across org rows: a delegation adopted at a parent organization never governs a child organization's acts whatever its org_node_id. | D4.10 | Frontline design review workflow (maintenance/operators/constructors)    | I.25      | ✅     | The workflow runs end-to-end and is CONSEQUENTIAL. design_studies EXTENDED to case scope (20261205090000:1) — the third I.25 discipline arrives as constructor_participated, and all three flags are now DERIVED from `design_study_participants` (20261205090000:428), who was in the room BY NAME and discipline; a case-bound study that types a flag with nobody behind it is refused for EVERY writer (enforce_case_study_derivation, smoke step 1). The eight I.25 dimensions are itemized findings on `design_review_findings` (20261205090000:508), each raised by somebody the roster records as present, in the discipline they attended as — refused at the door AND at the wall (enforce_design_finding_from_participant); a person on the roster twice is refused with the ambiguity named rather than filed as one discipline. DESIGN-LOCK GATING, through the SHIPPED machinery and NOT a second evaluator: `case_frontline_design_obligations` (20261205090000:1749) is the ONE predicate with four consumers — appended into case_gate_outstanding_obligations by transformation (raises if the anchor is gone), so get_gate_readiness renders it, enforce_gate_review_outstanding_obligations refuses over it for every writer, and record_case_gate_review trips that wall. Three families: an unanswered recommendation, an accepted recommendation no requirement carries, and a review of an I.25 kind with nobody in the room. Full chain: Case Workspace frontline section (src/components/develop/FrontlineDesignPanels.tsx:136, routed via DevelopmentCaseWorkspacePage.tsx:2874) → `record_case_design_study` / `add_design_study_participant` / `raise_design_review_finding` → rows under org-scoped RLS (definer-RPC-only, restrictive no-write policies on the case side) → `get_case_frontline_review` (20261205090000:2021), which REFUSES over an empty study set and over an empty finding set rather than reporting 0 open findings, with the counts null and not zero (`readFrontlineReview`, src/lib/design/index.ts:476). §70: no AI identity records a study, attends, raises or dispositions — refused by name at four doors and at the table for every writer. Residual, named not silent: a case with NO design review recorded at all is not blocked by this file. Making ABSENCE block a design-stage gate is the governance-intensity family's act (D3.16 / composite authority rules), and taking it here would re-decide another slice's contract from inside this one — the same refusal 20261122090300 made for assurance_not_satisfied. REPAIRED after adversarial review: `design_studies` — the PARENT of all three ledgers — carried no DELETE, TRUNCATE or frozen-link guard, so one `delete from design_studies` walked through all three children's mid-cascade escapes at once and cleared every blocker with them; `enforce_case_study_immutable` (20261205090000:961) now refuses that, refuses detaching the case and re-kinding the study, and TRUNCATE is revoked, with the genuine case cascade admitted AND recorded. And the SURFACE now admits the people the server does: the three frontline RPCs are the only ones in the migration tree that admit `supervisor`/`technician` by name, and the panel gated them on the workspace's `canPlan` — which excludes both and includes `ai_admin` — so every control was hidden from exactly the roles D4.10 exists to give a voice and shown to the one identity §70 refuses. `FRONTLINE_ROLES` (DevelopmentCaseWorkspacePage.tsx:130) now mirrors the RPCs, pinned by a test. | D4.11 | Frontline recommendation disposition record (who accepted/rejected, why) | I.25      | ✅     | The accountability record exists as ROWS, not aggregates. `design_finding_dispositions` (20261205090000:577): who answered, in which of the four disciplines (the three I.25 frontline ones plus engineering — the design authority answers the room, it does not attend as frontline), which of the three I.25 outcomes (accepted / rejected / accepted_with_conditions), and a reason that is NOT NULL and length-checked ON EVERY OUTCOME — an acceptance nobody explained is a promise nobody can check. Conditions exist exactly when the outcome is conditional, both directions refused. The raiser CANNOT answer their own finding (`disposition_design_finding` 20261205090000:1507 at the door, enforce_disposition_integrity at the wall) — the author-is-not-assurer rule this platform already enforces on assurance reviews. Append-only and numbered: a revision SUPERSEDES and the earlier answer stays visible, with audit_events carrying previous_state AND new_state; UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE are refused for every caller including the service path. The old findings_count / findings_closed aggregates (20260818090000:156) are no longer a second answer: on a case-bound study they are DERIVED from these rows by trigger and a typed value is refused. CONSEQUENTIAL: an un-dispositioned finding blocks every gate on the case, and an ACCEPTED recommendation that no design requirement carries KEEPS blocking until `carry_design_finding_to_requirement` links it — accepting it in the room and never building it is the failure I.25 exists to stop, and the link is refused before a disposition exists. Full chain: FrontlineDesignPanels.tsx:136 → developService.dispositionDesignFinding / carryDesignFindingToRequirement → definer RPC → RLS row → get_case_frontline_review readback with every disposition and its reason on screen. §70: an AI-recorded frontline opinion is refused by name at the door and for EVERY writer at the table. REPAIRED after adversarial review, four ways. (a) THE SCRIBE: `raised_by` may name somebody other than the caller — recording for the room is ordinary — and the raiser-≠-dispositioner wall compared the ATTRIBUTED raiser, so one person could put a recommendation in a colleague's mouth and then answer it themselves, with nothing anywhere recording who typed it. `recorded_by` is NOT NULL, is `auth.uid()`, is frozen, is in the audit `new_state`, is on the screen when it differs, and BARS the scribe from dispositioning. (b) THE DISCIPLINE CLAIM: `disposition_discipline` is the sentence "maintenance accepted this" and was a free choice among four while `raised_by_discipline` was read from the roster; a frontline discipline now requires having attended in it (door and wall), with `engineering` exempt because the design authority answers the room rather than attending it. (c) MEMBERSHIP: `dispositioned_by`/`scored_by` were unchecked, so §70 reduced to string equality against a profile that need not exist — an identity with NO `user_profiles` row (an unprovisioned system account) answered a maintainer, and a foreign tenant's member did too and was then rendered onto this tenant's screen; both are refused and every name join is tenant-scoped. (d) A CARRIER THAT CARRIES NOTHING: the blocker cleared on `requirement_id` alone, so an acceptance could be discharged onto a requirement whose verification had FAILED; `carry_design_finding_to_requirement` (20261205090000:1639) refuses a non-acceptance and a failed/waived carrier, and a fourth family `frontline_acceptance_carried_by_failed_requirement` re-blocks the gate when a carrier goes terminal-bad afterwards. Plus a provenance backstop (`record_frontline_service_write`, 20261205090000:389): the service-path writes these walls ADMIT used to leave nothing at all. | D4.12 | Six-axis design scoring (constructability/operability…)                  | I.26      | ✅     | The six I.26 axes VERBATIM — design_readiness, constructability, operability, maintainability, reliability, commissionability — as `design_axis_scores` (20261205090100:116), each scored 1–5 by a named human with a NOT NULL, length-checked basis; append-only, a re-score supersedes and the earlier judgement stays visible. THE REFUSAL, in allocateAvailability's idiom (src/lib/design/index.ts:65): `get_case_design_scorecard` (20261205090100:364) REFUSES the composite while ANY axis is unscored and NAMES the axis, and the mean of the axes that do have scores appears nowhere in the payload — it would read highest exactly when the missing axis is the bad one, because the axis nobody scored is usually the axis nobody owns. Five-of-six scored is proven to refuse live (smoke step 6), and the sixth produces the composite beside the WEAKEST axis, which is the part an average hides. ONE composite, computed server-side so the screen and the lineage row are the same number; `readDesignScorecard` (src/lib/design/index.ts:693) does not recompute it and adds a client-side BACKSTOP that refuses a composite arriving beside an unscored axis. D11.29: `compute_case_design_scorecard` records a calculation_runs row pinned to 'case_design_scorecard' / develop-design/5B/2026-12-05 — INCLUDING when it refuses (status refused, outputs null, the refusal in refusals). Full chain: FrontlineDesignPanels.tsx:125 scorecard section → `score_design_axis` / compute_case_design_scorecard → RLS rows → the six-axis readback. §70: scoring a design is refused to the AI-operator identity by name at the door and for every writer at the table. Residuals, named: this file gives the scorecard NO gate consequence — a threshold that blocks would be inventing governance policy the specification does not state, which is D3.16's act. assessStandardisation (E8.06) still has zero callers; it is the enterprise register's row and no axis here fabricates a score from it. REPAIRED: `scored_by` carried no tenant-membership check, so a design was scored by an identity with no `user_profiles` row and by another tenant's member, whose email the unscoped name join then rendered onto this tenant's scorecard; both refused, the join scoped. `score_design_axis` admits `supervisor`/`technician` by name — operability and maintainability are precisely the axes the people who will run and maintain the thing are qualified to score — and the panel gated the scoring form on `canPlan`, which excludes both; it is on the frontline capability now. The panel also CALLED `compute_case_design_scorecard` on mount — appending a D11.29 lineage row per page view, and blanking the whole panel for a supervisor or technician, whom that RPC's narrower role set refuses — so it now READS with `get_case_design_scorecard` and records a run on an explicit act, as every other develop panel does. The overlap-map ruling is "`design_requirements` is the ONE project requirement table" and this EXTENDS it. **Eleven categories:** `sync_spec10_requirement_categories` names the eleven and the CHECK is the UNION of those and the five E8.01 categories this table predates §10 with — mapping `sparing` onto QUALITY would be a silent guess inside a governance model, so a requirement outside the eleven is REPORTED, never rewritten. Reported by BOTH reporters this row names: `get_case_requirement_traceability`'s `gaps.outsideSpec10Taxonomy`, RENDERED on the panel, and the Requirements Agent's `outside_spec10_taxonomy` family. Before the repair both were absent — the list was computed and rendered nowhere and the agent had no such family, so the row claimed two reporters and there were zero. **Hierarchy:** `parent_requirement_id` with `enforce_requirement_hierarchy_integrity` refusing a self-parent, a cycle, a cross-org parent, a cross-case parent AND (repair) a move that would STRAND this row's children on the case it is leaving — the shipped trigger returned early for a row with no parent of its own, so moving a ROOT left its children behind while the row claimed "every writer, no service escape". INSERT and UPDATE, no marker. **Traceability:** the §10 thread reuses canonical stores only — objective→`risk_objectives`, installed asset→`assets`, commissioning test→acceptance_tests, operating KPI→kpi_catalog — with `enforce_requirement_thread_tenancy` refusing every cross-tenant link a foreign key cannot see. `link_requirement_thread` re-points and REFUSES to clear by name; §70 refuses `ai_admin` BY NAME (repair — see D12.09). The panel now offers an INSTALLED-ASSET and a COMMISSIONING-TEST selector: without them two of the four thread columns were write-unreachable from the product and `threadCoveragePct` was structurally pinned at 0% for any customer data while rendering as a measured figure. **Reconciled with Slice 4A, not duplicated:** ONE requirement concept carries both chains — `scope_need_id` is its upstream in the I.6 scope chain, `objective_id` its upstream in the §10 thread — and the report DELEGATES "which requirements are absent from the WBS" to `get_case_scope_traceability` (D5.02). **Refusal-first, and the repair made three absences honest:** over an empty requirement set it REFUSES rather than reporting zero orphans; Spec I.6 built in the spec's own order — business need (`project_scope_needs`, owner NOT NULL, eight-tier source_authority, ai_admin capped at AI_SUGGESTION) → requirement (design_requirements EXTENDED with scope_need_id — the ONE requirement table, no fork) → system (organizations at org_level='system', the ONE five-level tree; a node outside the tenant's subtree is refused via org_node_in_scope) → WBS (`project_wbs_elements`, parent hierarchy, derived depth) → cost (`project_cost_items`, D5.29) → control account (`project_control_accounts` — the WBS x OBS x CBS intersection, accountable_owner_id NOT NULL). | D5.05 | Earned value metric suite (CPI/SPI/EV/ES/EAC/VAC)                             | I.8        | ✅     | THE SUITE COMPUTES AND EVERY METRIC REFUSES BY NAME (20261201090300). `get_case_earned_value` is the ONE predicate; `compute_case_earned_value` is the same answer plus its lineage row, and the surface renders the RUN. EV IS CUMULATIVE TO THE DATA DATE — Σ over the LATEST recorded position PER ELEMENT at or before the period end of (percent DERIVED from the cited rule of credit) × (baselined cost of that element AND its subtree) — not a sum over the rows typed into the latest period: `record_progress_claim` allows one claim per element per period and offers no carry-forward, so summing the period's rows silently dropped every element that did not move and manufactured a cost overrun out of ordinary reporting practice ('claim what moved'). How many positions were carried forward is stated in a caveat, and `claimCount` (positions the total is made of) and `claimsInLatestPeriod` are reported separately because they are different facts; PV = the period's planned percent × BAC; AC = Σ recorded actuals on the §23 cost lines; CPI = EV/AC; SPI = EV/PV; ES interpolated on the planned curve in periods with SPI(t) = ES/AT; EAC = BAC/CPI; VAC = BAC − EAC. THE FORBIDDEN DEFAULTS ARE EACH WALLED AND EACH PROVEN LIVE: an empty claim set refuses ('not nothing earned — indistinguishable from a project that genuinely earned nothing'); a missing actual refuses AC/CPI/EAC/VAC rather than coalescing to 0 ('would report infinite cost efficiency on a project nobody has costed'); a zero or absent PV refuses SPI instead of producing Infinity; a zero or absent BAC refuses every ratio derived from it; a claim on a WBS element AND something inside it refuses EV by name because an element's budget includes its subtree; a claim set whose elements ALL carry no baselined cost anywhere in their subtree refuses EV rather than summing to zero, because a zero EV against a positive AC prints CPI 0.000 — the most alarming statement earned value can make, produced by arithmetic performed on nothing and indistinguishable on screen from a real collapse (the mirror image of 'CPI 1.0 over an empty set'), and a partial one carries a caveat naming how many; earned schedule refuses BELOW the first planned point for the same reason it refuses above the last one, because reading below the start means interpolating from an assumed origin at period zero and zero percent, which is a planned point nobody recorded; a case whose lines are in two currencies has no total and the refusal NAMES the currencies. Every numeric is tested for non-finiteness by explicit literal comparison (`= 'NaN'::numeric`), because NaN equals NaN in Postgres and every ordinary comparison against it is false. EAC NAMES ITS FORMULA ON THE NUMBER, every time — `EAC = BAC / CPI (past cost performance continues)` — and REFUSES when CPI is absent rather than falling back to `AC + (BAC − EV)`: a forecast that silently changes its own definition keeps its shape while changing its meaning. RULING on the data date (stated in the migration): actual cost is a running total on project_cost_items (spec §23) and this slice does not fork a time-phased actuals ledger, so the suite computes at the LATEST period only — a back-dated CPI would pair a past period's earned value with today's actuals. Historic performance is read from recorded runs (D5.06), never recomputed, and a suite computed at a CLOSED latest period says so in a caveat — the claims are frozen while actual cost keeps accruing, so it is today's cost against a stopped position and the trend refuses to file it as that period's history. STALENESS SEES AMOUNTS, NOT COUNTS: `get_case_earned_value` returns a `basisDigest` over the cost lines' baselined/actual/forecast figures, the cumulative claimed percents and the planned point, and `earnedValueFingerprint` compares the recorded digest against it — `record_cost_item` revises baseline_cost and actual IN PLACE (actual is a running total by design, §23), so a fingerprint of row counts left a three-times-wrong EAC on screen captioned 'recorded … code version …'. Every metric refusal is recorded on the run under that metric's own label, so the cell shows the reason the calculation gave rather than accusing the lineage ledger of not recording one. Surface: `src/components/develop/PerformancePanels.tsx` (EarnedValueSection) → computeCaseEarnedValue → `get_case_performance`; pure helpers and their refusal paths in `src/lib/develop/performance.ts` — `metricDisplay` renders from a recorded run and NEVER from the live read (it reads the run's own label-prefixed refusal for the reason), and its unit tests cover every way a metric can be absent. The per-element budgets beside the grid and both confidence chips are rendered from the RUN too — a money aggregate or a rating taken from the live read would sit un-lineaged and current beside a metric grid that may be stale, indistinguishable on screen. | D5.06 | Performance trending and rules-of-credit suite                                | I.8        | ✅     | RULES OF CREDIT ARE THE OBJECT, AND A PERCENT CANNOT BE TYPED (20261201090000, 20261201090300). `project_rules_of_credit` records, per work type, the ordered earning steps and their weights; `enforce_rule_of_credit` refuses — for EVERY writer, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE — a step with no label, a non-finite weight, and weights that do not sum to exactly 100 ('a rule that does not add to the whole caps or inflates every element it governs, and nothing downstream would say why'). Two rules for one work type are refused because that would make 'which rule applies' a choice made at claim time, which is a percent chosen at claim time — AND SO IS THE WORK TYPE ITSELF, so it is an attribute of the ELEMENT and never of the claim: `project_wbs_elements.work_type` is recorded once by `set_wbs_element_work_type` (§70-walled, basis mandatory, immutable once the element carries a claim) and both `record_progress_claim` and `enforce_progress_claim` RESOLVE THE RULE FROM THE ELEMENT. A claim against an untyped element is refused by name, and a claim citing a rule whose work type is not the element's is refused for every writer including the service path — without that arm the derivation is honest and its input is a free parameter, which lands in the same place. A rule is also immutable once claims cite it (steps, work type and method frozen, for every writer) and it is not deletable by a client, because a deleted rule takes the immutability refusal with it. `record_progress_claim` takes a STEP INDEX and no percent parameter exists; `trg_progress_claim` RE-DERIVES claimed_percent and step_label from the cited rule for every writer, so a service caller writing 99 directly still stores what the rule earns (proven live). PROGRESS CLAIMED WITH NO APPLICABLE RULE OF CREDIT IS REFUSED BY NAME — not zero, not full credit. TRENDING IS OVER RECORDED PERIODS: `get_case_performance_trend` reads the `case_earned_value` run recorded while each period was current — matched on the run's own recorded periodRef AND recorded at or before the instant that period CLOSED, because claims freeze on close while the cost ledger does not, so without that predicate a run computed afterwards became the closed period's history and the recorded point moved whenever somebody revised a cost line. A period with no MEASURED run is a GAP that says which kind it is — nobody computed it, its only run refused, or its only runs came after the close — rather than being interpolated across ('an interpolated point is a measurement nobody took, drawn on the same axis as ones they did'), and `compute_case_performance_trend` records a run whose input_refs ARE the calculation_runs rows it read. A REFUSED run is not a measured point (`refusedPointCount` is reported separately) because a period that measured nothing must not be presented as one that did. A direction needs two measured points; one is a position — and the direction reported is the direction of the LAST measured interval, named with the two periods it spans, because a first-versus-last comparison ignored everything between and reported shapes the series never had; a series whose slope changes sign carries a volatility note, and an ABSENT direction is refused by name rather than dropped from the sentence (`trendSentence` in `src/lib/develop/performance.ts`). A closed period is history — no claims, no curve edits, no re-opening, walled for client AND service. §70: the AI-operator identity is refused BY NAME from claiming progress, from authoring a rule of credit (the convention decides the answer before any claim is made), from recording an element's work type (which selects the convention), from setting the planned curve (which IS the time-phased cost baseline), and from BOTH ENDS of the reporting period — closing one fixes the position, and opening the next moves the data date every metric is computed at, which un-fixes it. RULINGS in the migration: one claimed position per element per period; credit MAY go backwards and is reported as a regression rather than refused. Surface: `src/components/develop/PerformancePanels.tsx` (RulesOfCreditSection, ProgressSection, TrendSection) → recordRuleOfCredit / setWbsElementWorkType / recordProgressClaim / openProgressPeriod / setPeriodPlannedProgress / closeProgressPeriod / computeCasePerformanceTrend → `get_case_performance`. The claim form has no work-type field and no percent field: it shows the type recorded on the element and the rule that resolves from it. | D5.07 | Probabilistic forecast presentation (P50/P80 beside deterministic)            | I.9        | ✅     | THE DISTRIBUTION NOW EXISTS, SO THE PERCENTILES DO (20261202090200). Slice 4B shipped this row 🟡 with the P50/P80 columns saying ABSENT rather than printing a spread nobody simulated; 4C supplies the binding that was named as the gap. `record_case_schedule_simulation` stores one `schedule_simulation_runs` row per simulation — seed, iteration count, kernel version, the DIGEST of the exact inputs it consumed, the §50 score that permitted it, P10/P50/P80/P90 off one sorted sample, the P50/P80 finish dates and the cost pair — and `get_case_forecast_confidence` reads the percentiles off that row and off nothing else. `percentileCell` in `src/lib/develop/performance.ts` is still the ONE place an absence is rendered and still has no branch that derives a percentile from a deterministic figure; the slice test asserts no such arithmetic exists in the SQL either (no `deterministic * n`, no default variance, no hardcoded interval). WHAT IS PROVED BY THE RECORD, STATED PLAINLY: the kernel runs on the CLIENT, so the server does not re-execute the sampler — what it does is pin the inputs by digest and REFUSE a result whose declared digest does not match, re-run the quality gate itself, and record the seed, so anybody holding the ledger row can re-run the kernel and get the same numbers or prove they cannot. THE DATE RULING: the simulation measures a DURATION, so the P50/P80 finish are the plan's own latest planned finish shifted by the overrun the simulation found, stated on the number; with no planned finish the percentiles are reported in hours and the DATE is refused. STALENESS IS THE OTHER HALF: a recorded run whose input digest no longer matches is reported `current: false` and its percentiles are NOT offered as the forecast — 'a P80 a schedule change has already invalidated is more dangerous than no P80, because it is specific' — and `forecastConfidenceFingerprint` gained `distributionExists` and `simulationId` because the old counts could not see a NEW simulation. Surface: `ForecastConfidenceSection` in `src/components/develop/PerformancePanels.tsx`. Transcript: `scripts/ci-develop-slice4c-smoke.sh` step 9. REPAIRED BY ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (20261202090300): four ways of showing a percentile nobody simulated are now closed, each with a live round-trip in the transcript rather than a sentence in the migration. (1) THE §50 GATE IS CHECKED WHERE THE NUMBER IS SERVED, not only where it is recorded — a schedule that degraded after a run was recorded kept serving that P80 with `current: true`; `get_case_forecast_confidence` now requires exists AND current AND gate-permitted and names which of the three is missing (smoke step 9c drives P6's float negative, which the digest deliberately does not hash, so the ONLY reason to withhold is the gate). (2) `planned_start`/`planned_finish` JOINED THE DIGEST: they are the calendar anchor of the P50/P80 dates, and without them a re-dated schedule served a P80 date 78 days BEFORE the deterministic finish, labelled current (step 9b). (3) `deterministicHours` is BOUNDED BY THE NETWORK — at least the longest activity, at most all of them end to end, which needs no second critical path — because it alone shifts both published dates and 99999 produced a completion date in 2016 (step 8b). (4) A STALE RUN'S PERCENTILES ARE NOT RENDERED AT ALL: `percentileCell` used to receive the recorded number regardless, so a superseded P80 rendered in the same bright style as a current one with a collapsed details block as the only signal. The cost half is stated as what it is — deterministic EAC plus sampled exposure — because the old sentence denied it. | D5.08 | Risk-to-schedule-to-economics linkage model                                   | I.10       | ✅     | THE I.10 CHAIN IS ONE RELATION BETWEEN TWO CANONICAL STORES (20261202090100). `risk_schedule_impacts` joins `risks` (the ISO 31000 spine, overlap-map ruling on §12) to `shutdown_tasks` (the D5.28 ScheduleActivity) and creates no risk store, no schedule store and no third place to type a probability. THE PROBABILITY RULING IS THE HARD ONE AND IT IS IN THE MIGRATION: `risks.likelihood` is an UNBOUNDED score (`check (likelihood >= 0)`), not a probability, so reading one as the other — dividing by 5, or by 100 — would silently invent the number that decides how often a risk happens at all; the LINK carries its own `probability` in (0,1] with a mandatory basis, and the slice test asserts no arithmetic anywhere converts the register score. THE SPREAD IS REFUSED AT THE INPUT END: the delay is a three-point range in days, ordered, and `constraint rsi_delay_is_a_range` refuses a triple whose ends meet ('a point estimate with three columns') at the SCHEMA, not only in the act — the cheapest place to manufacture a distribution is at data entry, where it looks like diligence. Direct cost is three points and a currency or nothing at all. THE DAYS→MONEY HOP uses the canonical numeric-assumption store per ruling 5 (`financial_assumptions` under the published `sync_case_delay_cost_key` key, written through the existing `upsert_financial_assumption`, which already demands a source) rather than a new column, and where no rate exists `get_case_delay_cost_rate` REFUSES BY NAME — I.10's chain honestly truncated, not silently completed at a default rate. `get_case_risk_schedule_chain` walks risk → activity → milestone → money one row per edge and NAMES the open risks that name no activity rather than counting them. §70 refuses the AI-operator identity by name and it is absent from the allowed-role list. The chain now excludes them, NAMES the excluded edges (`retiredLinkNote`, surfaced on the panel), and the risk digest follows the same population so retiring a risk marks the recorded run stale instead of leaving it silently sampled. §70 also now refuses the AI identity on `record_local_schedule_relationship` and on all three compute recorders: authoring the logic the gate is computed over IS accepting a schedule, and one AI-authored relationship was proven to move the gate from permitted to refused. | D5.09 | Integrated risk-cost-schedule Monte Carlo attribution (per-risk P80 days + $) | I.10       | ✅     | MARGINAL, MEASURED, AND OUT OF THE SIMULATION ITSELF (`src/lib/modelling/integrated-risk.ts`, 20261202090200). The kernel is EXTENDED, never duplicated: the critical path is `criticalPath` from `src/lib/modelling/schedule-risk.ts`, and the RNG, the triangular sampler and the percentile function are `src/lib/modelling/random.ts`, and the slice test asserts no sampling machinery exists in SQL. What is new is the risk layer — a risk occurs at its own recorded probability, adds a triangularly sampled delay to the activity it NAMES, and costs money directly and through the days. ATTRIBUTION IS THE SAME RUN RE-EXECUTED WITH ONE RISK SUPPRESSED, so the ranking comes out of the simulation rather than an assumed ordering, and it answers I.10 in the spec's own shape ('X contributes 17 days of P80 schedule exposure and $14.2M of expected economic exposure' — `attributionSentence`). THE COMMON-RANDOM-NUMBERS DEFECT THIS SLICE FOUND AND FIXED: with one shared stream, a risk consumed a VARIABLE number of draws per iteration, so suppressing it also re-randomised everything after it — a risk on an activity with 260 hours of float measured a tenth of a day of pure stream displacement, and a risk with probability 1e-12 moved the P80 by six hours while never occurring. Each source now draws from its OWN stream, seeded from the one recorded seed mixed with a stable key (FNV-1a folded into a splitmix avalanche — never seed-plus-index, which is correlated in mulberry32's first outputs), and each risk draws a FIXED number of values whether it occurs or not. The kernel unit suite asserts that a suppressed risk changes nothing else and that the attribution is byte-reproducible, without which drivers would be ranked by sampling noise — a unit test is not evidence a customer can reach this, so the reachable chain is stated separately: `simulateIntegratedRisk` is the entry point, called by `runCaseScheduleSimulation` in `src/services/developService.ts`, which `src/components/develop/SchedulePanels.tsx` invokes from the Simulate control and which posts to `record_case_schedule_simulation`. Marginal contributions are NOT normalised to sum to the total — risks interact through the network, and normalising would make the numbers agree and stop them being true; the run records that as a refusal. The door verifies every attributed risk is an edge that exists ('an assumed ordering wearing a computed one's clothes'). Transcript: `scripts/ci-develop-slice4c-smoke.sh` steps 6, 7 and 10. REPAIRED (20261202090300): the door checked WHICH RISK IDS appeared and not one number. A row reading `occurrenceRate: 9.9, p80DaysContribution: 4200, meanCostContribution: 777000000, riskTitle: 'WHATEVER I WANT'` was accepted verbatim and rendered as '…currently contributes 4200.0 day(s) of P80 schedule exposure and 777,000,000 of expected economic exposure' — the assumed ordering the door's own error string names. Every row is now bounded by the run it claims to come from: occurrence rate in [0,1], hours contribution within the run's own P90, days equal to hours/24 within tolerance, money within the run's recorded exposure, and the RISK TITLE taken from `risks.title` server-side. The `criticality` array — the driver list §51 shows whenever a case has no risk edges — was not validated at all and is now: every id must be an activity on this case, the index must be a share, and the array is bounded. `attributionSentence` prints '(currency not established)' rather than an unlabelled money figure. | D5.13 | Schedule quality diagnostics (nine defect classes)                            | II.6       | ✅     | ALL NINE II.6 CLASSES DIAGNOSED, AND THE ONES THE DATA CANNOT ANSWER SAY SO (20261202090000). `get_case_schedule_quality` reports missing logic, open ends, excessive constraints, long-duration activities, negative float, unrealistic lags, broken critical path, excessive concurrency and unrealistic calendars over the D5.28 activity set, each with its count, its denominator, its published threshold and a severity. Rulings the spec leaves open are decided IN THE MIGRATION: missing logic is an activity with NEITHER side and open ends one with exactly one (disjoint populations, so nothing is counted twice); durations are ELAPSED hours because the import refuses to convert P6 units, so the long-duration limit is 1056 h; a calendar is judged by the arithmetic it implies (a duration exceeding its own window, or exactly filling one longer than a week) and NEVER by its name; and float and constraints are P6-OWNED — `total_float_hours`, `constraint_type`, `constraint_date` and relationship `link_type`/`lag_hours` now ride the ONE governed import door with named refusals for a non-finite float, a dateless date constraint and a lag annotating a predecessor the row never declared. Recomputing the network here would have been a second critical path beside the one in `src/lib/modelling/schedule-risk.ts`, so P6's own answers are imported instead (spec §22/§77) and the three new columns join the P6 field wall on INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE (`enforce_schedule_activity_provenance`) — a client that could edit `total_float_hours` could clear a negative-float finding and open the Monte Carlo gate by typing. THE LOAD-BEARING BEHAVIOUR IS THAT A BLIND CLASS IS NOT A PASS: `sync_schedule_defect_class` returns severity `not_diagnosable` with a NAMED reason ('re-export with total_float_hours', 'the export did not include the lag column', 'the calendar NAME is recorded and is not evidence'), contributes NO weight to §50, and is rendered grey rather than green in `src/components/develop/SchedulePanels.tsx`. Surfaces: Schedule quality section → `get_case_schedule_quality` / `computeCaseScheduleQuality`. Transcript: `scripts/ci-develop-slice4c-smoke.sh` steps 1-3. REPAIRED (20261202090300): `shutdown_task_dependencies` was promoted into gate-determining status by this slice (link type and lag feed four of the nine classes) and kept one SELECT policy, no trigger of any kind, and TRUNCATE granted to anon, authenticated and service_role — while the activity table beside it got the full wall on the reasoning that a client who could edit `total_float_hours` could clear a negative-float finding by typing. Deleting a relationship clears an open-ends finding the same way. The logic ledger now has the provenance trigger on INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, the statement-level TRUNCATE guard, the revoked grant, the P6 field wall for logic on imported activities, and §70. | D5.14 | Schedule Confidence Score                                                     | II.6       | ✅     | A DIFFERENT QUESTION FROM QUALITY, WITH ITS OWN FOUR COMPONENTS (20261202090000). Quality asks whether the schedule is built correctly; confidence asks how much weight it will BEAR, and a structurally perfect schedule imported once, never updated, carrying no duration ranges and coded to no authorized scope justifies very little. So `get_case_schedule_quality` also composes structure (the §50 score, 40), uncertainty expressed (what share of activities carry an optimistic AND pessimistic duration at all, 25), import history (how many accepted import runs have landed on this case — one load is a snapshot with no track record, credit capped at three, 15) and scope anchoring (what share resolve to a WBS element, 20). Each component travels with its own BASIS sentence, so a low rating names which leg is short. It is REFUSED whenever the quality score is refused — 'a confidence rating built on an unscored schedule would be a second number carrying the first number's problem while looking like an independent opinion' — and the smoke asserts the two numbers are not equal, so the confidence cannot be quality wearing another label. It travels with the §51 forecast as `scheduleConfidence` (20261202090200) because a percentile is worth what the schedule it came off is worth. ONE implementation shared with the §50 row above, as that row required. There is no 'run anyway with a caveat' arm anywhere, because a caveated P80 and a clean P80 are read identically by the person the paper is written for; the kernel refuses in the same words (`simulateIntegratedRisk` returns `simulated: false` before sampling anything) and `src/components/develop/SchedulePanels.tsx` does not render the Simulate control at all. The caller cannot supply the threshold or the score either. | D5.17 | Estimate confidence rating on forecasts                                       | II.7       | ✅     | DERIVED, NEVER DECLARED, AND IT TRAVELS (20261201090100). There is no confidence column on project_estimate_basis and no parameter through which any caller can state one: `estimate_confidence_rating` — an INTERNAL helper with no EXECUTE for anyone (its only callers are the definers in this slice that scope the case to the caller's org first) and carrying 20261130090700's dual-caller `auth.uid()` gate in its own body, so neither a direct PostgREST call nor a future re-grant can hand a tenant another tenant's estimate defence — derives the band from the eight dimensions by a stated, deterministic mapping — class 1-2 high, class 3 medium, class 4-5 low, one band down for each of (under half priced from measured quantities · vendor pricing no stronger than indicative · scope at concept or feasibility maturity) — and returns the MAPPING and the DRIVERS with the rating so a reader can disagree with it explicitly (spec §46's 'do not pretend universal science'). The band NEVER rises above its class; the slice test asserts no `v_score + 1` exists. UNRATED IS NOT LOW: with no basis record the band is `unrated` with a named refusal, because LOW is a finding about a weak estimate and unrated is the absence of any finding, and one word for both would let 'nobody wrote the basis down' read as 'we assessed it and it is poor'. `confidenceLabel` in `src/lib/develop/performance.ts` prints a different word and tone for each, with unit tests. THE RATING TRAVELS WITH THE NUMBER: `get_case_earned_value` embeds it, `compute_case_earned_value` records an UNRATED estimate as a refusal on the lineage row, and `get_case_forecast_confidence` carries it as §51's fourth field on both the cost and the schedule forecast. `compute_case_estimate_confidence` records its own run (key `case_estimate_confidence`) with the drivers as OUTPUTS and a refusal only when the band fell below its class — recording the drivers as refusals made `status='computed'` unreachable and turned the run's refusal signal into noise, which is the mirror image of recording only successes. Surface: the confidence chip on the estimate-basis, earned-value and forecast sections of `src/components/develop/PerformancePanels.tsx` — each rendered from the RECORDED run, never from the live read, because a chip that could read HIGH with no run behind it is the silently confident number this row exists to prevent. | D5.18 | Contingency ledger with authority-gated drawdown                              | II.8       | ✅     | Contingency is a LEDGER (20261203090000). `project_contingency_pools` anchors a fund to ONE approved COST baseline with its original amount, currency and stated basis; `contingency_ledger_entries` is append-only and every drawdown records its cause, its approver, the CEILING that approver was checked against and the balance it left. Nine rulings are enforced and stated in the migration: (R1) NO ADOPTED `contingency_drawdown` DELEGATION REFUSES — the deliberate opposite of `enforce_authority_limit`'s "the organization has not delegated in amounts yet" pass, because "nobody has said how much you may spend" cannot mean "spend what you like"; (R2) a NULL `max_commitment_usd` REFUSES — unstated is not unlimited; (R3) a drawdown above the remainder refuses naming it, and `check (balance_after >= 0)` holds for a service caller too; (R4) NaN/Infinity/negative/zero refused by `sync_finite_money` BEFORE any balance arithmetic ('NaN'::numeric = 'NaN' is TRUE in Postgres and passes every inequality vacuously); (R7) THE CEILING IS AN AMOUNT **IN A CURRENCY** — `authority_limits.max_commitment_currency` is stated beside it and a fund in another currency REFUSES, because Sync holds no exchange rate and comparing CAD to a USD ceiling is wrong in both directions (at ~1.37 a CAD 340,000 draw inside the delegation would be refused while a CAD 250,000 draw far under it would pass); (R8) THE CEILING IS CUMULATIVE AGAINST ONE FUND, NOT PER TRANSACTION — a $250,000 approver committed $500,000 in two calls seconds apart before this was enforced, so `sync_contingency_authority` now measures the approver's NET commitment against this pool and refuses naming what is already committed; (R12) a ROLE FLOOR on spending at least as tight as the floor on REPORTING the spend, because `authority_limits.role_key` is free text and a ladder adopted against a mistyped role granted spend authority to a role that could not run the consumption report; (R13) the pool row is `select … for update` BEFORE the balance is read — two concurrent drawdowns both passed the balance check and the double spend was blocked only by `unique (pool_id, entry_no)`, an index that exists for ordering. The ONE authority store gains `action_type='contingency_drawdown'` with the 20261121090100 §3 org-node scope rule repeated verbatim — no second authority store. §70 is in the door AND on the row — `enforce_contingency_entry_provenance` refuses an AI-identity approver AND `enforce_contingency_pool_wall` now covers **INSERT** as well as UPDATE and DELETE, which it did not at first: the pool was the one table in the slice with no INSERT-side check at all, and a service caller could mint a $50M fund against another case's superseded SCOPE baseline, established by the AI identity, unaudited, which `get_case_contingency` then reported as this tenant's remaining balance. The money fields are refused to EVERY caller including the audited service path (a superuser UPDATE moved a pool $1M→$9M in review before that wall existed), and so now are the CAUSE SUBJECT (`cause_risk_id`, `cause_change_id`) and the DELEGATION reference — re-pointing an entry at a different change closed that change's contingency obligation with money drawn for another one. A TARGETED **DELETE** of an entry or a pool is refused for every caller too: `sync_contingency_remaining` derives the balance from the entries, so deleting a $180,000 spend CREATED $180,000 of spendable authority while removing the audited row that would have shown it; the only admitted disappearance is the cascade from the development case itself, detected because the parent row is already gone, and that is audited. TRUNCATE refused at statement level and revoked from anon/authenticated/service_role. THE CEILING ITSELF IS NOW GOVERNED (20261203090400): it had no authoring surface (the seeds are null, R2 makes null refuse, and the refusal's own remediation was impossible through the product — only a DBA could enable the feature), no wall (`update authority_limits set max_commitment_usd = 250000000` succeeded with security_events and audit_events unchanged, and a drawdown under the silently raised ceiling was then recorded on an immutable ledger quoting it as if it had been checked) and no §70 refusal (the AI identity could adopt the very instrument that decides who may spend). `state_authority_ceiling` / `draft_authority_ceiling` / `get_authority_delegations` are that surface, `enforce_authority_limit_wall` is that wall (an adopted 4D delegation's ceiling, role, action type and scope are immutable for every caller; it is SUPERSEDED by adopting a replacement, never un-adopted or deleted), and `adopt_authority_limit` now refuses `ai_admin` and refuses adopting the ceiling of the role you hold. RULING 4D-R33, stated because it changes what the audit trail means: a BEFORE trigger that inserts a `security_events` row and then RAISES loses the insert with the statement — proven live — so no refusing path in this slice makes that call. The refusal is the enforcement and it is total; the rows that land are the ADMITTED service writes. RESIDUALS, NAMED: (a) a drawdown has no client-supplied idempotency key, so a retry after a timed-out-but-committed request would double-spend; (b) the adopted-ceiling wall and the no-un-adopt rule are scoped to the two action types 4D introduces — an adopted `sanction` or `gate_requirement_waiver` ladder can still have its ceiling rewritten or be returned to draft by a service caller, which is §41/§43's area and is left open rather than closed by editing those slices' transcripts. Full chain: Case Workspace → `ChangeAndControlsPanel` (src/components/develop/ChangeControlPanels.tsx, wired src/pages/DevelopmentCaseWorkspacePage.tsx) → `establishContingencyPool`/`drawDownContingency`/`releaseContingency` (src/services/developService.ts) → `establish_contingency_pool` / `draw_down_contingency` / `release_contingency` → rows under RLS → `get_case_contingency`. Full chain for the ceiling: `AuthorityDelegationSection` in `ChangeAndControlsPanel` → `stateAuthorityCeiling`/`draftAuthorityCeiling`/`adoptAuthorityLimit`/`getAuthorityDelegations` (src/services/developService.ts) → the 20261203090400 RPCs → `authority_limits` under RLS. | D5.20 | Progress integrity cross-check with confidence rating                         | II.9       | ✅     | THE SPEC'S OWN SENTENCE, PRODUCED FROM DATA (20261201090200). `project_progress_evidence` records independent COUNTED PAIRS — observed_complete of observed_total, with a unit and a mandatory basis — against the six II.9 sources (drawings issued, deliverables accepted, quantities complete, procurement releases, field installation, inspection records). RULING, stated in the migration: a source recordable as a bare percentage would be a second place to type a progress number, which is the hole this row exists to close; the denominator must be > 0 ('an observation out of nothing is a division by zero wearing a percentage sign'). `get_case_progress_integrity` rates THE SAME POPULATION THE MONEY WAS COMPUTED ON — the cumulative position per element at or before the data date (D5.05's ruling), with evidence taken as the latest observation per element per source at or before the same date — so 'this earned value carries a HIGH progress confidence' is a statement about the set the earned value actually used. It compares each claimed percent against the LOWEST independent observation for that element — the binding source is NAMED, so one generous source cannot cover a damning one — and bands the ABSOLUTE divergence (≤5 high, ≤15 medium, >15 low), because a signed test would let under-claiming pass as conservatism. THE THREE HONESTY RULES: an element with no observation is UNRATED, never HIGH ('nothing contradicts it and nothing confirms it, and those are not the same thing'); a case with NO evidence at all has no rating and the refusal says absence of evidence is not confirmation; COVERAGE travels with every rating ('this rating covers 1 of 2 claimed element(s)'). The live transcript produces spec II.9's own example from data: fabrication reported 100% complete while only 30 of 100 tonnes are erected → confidence LOW with the discrepancy named. The rating is a function, not a column: no RPC, parameter or column can state one. §70: recording an independent observation is refused to the AI-operator identity BY NAME — an identity that could write the evidence could verify the claim it is forbidden to make. Immutable, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE all walled (evidence that can be deleted stops contradicting a claim the moment it becomes inconvenient), TRUNCATE refused and revoked. THE EARNED VALUE CARRIES IT, AND CARRIES ITS COVERAGE: `compute_case_earned_value` records the progress confidence AND its coverage in its outputs and records a refusal both when the claims behind a figure were never cross-checked and whenever the coverage is below 100% — a HIGH band used to pass through silently, leaving a bare green chip on the earned-value and forecast panels, which is verbatim the failure Rule 3 above names. `coverageSuffix` in `src/lib/develop/performance.ts` puts the fraction on the chip itself. The read returns ONE definition of `evidenceCount` and a `basisDigest`, and both the recorded run and the surface read them from it — two definitions of that count made a just-recorded run read as permanently stale and suppressed its code-version caption for ever. Surface: `src/components/develop/PerformancePanels.tsx` (ProgressIntegritySection) → recordProgressEvidence / computeCaseProgressIntegrity → `get_case_performance`. | D5.27 | Change object with propagation chain                                          | III.§21    | ✅     | The Change object (§21) is `project_changes` (20261203090100) and it RIDES the existing MOC engine rather than forking it: its `change_class` must resolve to a rule in the MOC engine's own class table (extended with four project-delivery classes, not twinned — `enforce_project_change_governance` refuses an unknown class by name), its competence sign-off is that rule's required role, and `enforce_project_change_governance` refuses `status='approved'` with no sign-off for EVERY writer — the 20260809140000 sentence, enforced on this table for INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE. What the register named as missing is what is new: BASELINE ANCHORING (`baseline_id` NOT NULL, RESTRICT, must be a non-draft baseline OF THIS CASE — a draft still changes by being edited), the IMPACT VECTOR (technical/cost/schedule/risk/contingency effects, complete or the assessment did not happen — `project_change_assessment_complete`), AUTHORITY ROUTING (`authority_limits.action_type='change_approval'` on BOTH §43 dimensions, money and residual risk, with R1/R2 restated), and the PROPAGATION CHAIN (`project_change_propagation`, one row per downstream object). The chain's honesty is the design: `sync_owned` hops are applied by `propagate_project_change` and PROVEN from the target record (the scope hop stamps `approved_change_ref` through 20261130090400's own `app.scope_change_write` marker; the contingency hop closes only when a ledger drawdown cites this change), and every other hop is a NAMED OBLIGATION a human closes with a note — Sync is not the system of record for P6, the estimate or the drawing register and never marks a hop applied there. `close_change_propagation` refuses to hand-assert a Sync-owned hop. THE IMPACT VECTOR IS AUTHORED, NOT DEFAULTED. The Assess control first shipped posting a hardcoded vector — cost 0, schedule 0, risk Low, currency CAD, the note as both technical effect and impact basis — which made three of this row's claims false from the surface: authority routed on magnitude 0 so a $10M change was approvable under a $250k ceiling; all four auto-hops are gated on a non-zero effect, so the propagation chain this row is NAMED for had no writable path; and the 20-character impact-basis wall was satisfied by a literal the component supplied. The form now takes cost, contingency, schedule days, currency, residual risk, technical effect and impact basis, with NO defaults and no fallback literals. THE ANCHOR MUST STILL GOVERN: `draft` was refused but `superseded` was not, so a change could be raised, assessed, signed, approved and propagated against a document that had already been replaced — and `propagate_project_change` would have stamped its reference onto live post-baseline scope attribution, clearing spec I.7's "changed with no approved change request" signal on the authority of an obsolete anchor. Refused now at raise, on the row, and re-checked at the decision. A DECIDED CHANGE DOES NOT UN-DECIDE for any caller: the service path was admitted silently, and once un-decided the impact vector could be re-assessed smaller and the change re-approved under a LOWER ceiling while a recorded drawdown still cited it. A CLOSED PROPAGATION OBLIGATION DOES NOT REOPEN and `sync_owned` does not flip — a service caller could reopen every hop, forge a closure with a real manager's name on the contingency hop that `close_change_propagation` reserves to "the record that proves it", and `implement_project_change`'s "nothing outstanding" gate then passed with nothing behind the claim. RESIDUAL, NAMED AND NOT PAPERED OVER: the MOC class table itself is seeded by provisioning and has no authoring surface — an organization cannot yet add its own change class through the product, and the reachability gate correctly refuses a table citation for it. That is a gap on the MOC engine this row EXTENDS, not on the change object it builds; the four project-delivery classes ship as seeds exactly as the four asset classes did in 20260809140000, and the act that CONSUMES the rule — `sign_project_change_engineering` (surface `signProjectChangeEngineering` in the Change section of `ChangeAndControlsPanel`) — is fully reachable and refuses a signer who does not hold the required role. Full chain: `ChangeAndControlsPanel` → `raiseProjectChange`/`assessProjectChange`/`propagateProjectChange` → the RPCs → rows under RLS → `get_case_change_control`. | D5.31 | Schedule Quality Score §50                                                    | III.§50    | ✅     | THE SIX §50 COMPONENTS, PUBLISHED WEIGHTS, AND A REFUSAL WHERE A SCORE WOULD BE A LIE (20261202090000). `sync_schedule_quality_policy()` is the one server-side, immutable home for the weights (logic completeness 20, open ends 20, constraints 15, duration quality 15, critical-path continuity 20, calendar consistency 10 — summing to 100, asserted), the per-class thresholds and the floors; `SCHEDULE_QUALITY_POLICY` in `src/lib/develop/schedule.ts` mirrors it and the slice test pins every value, so a threshold cannot be widened on one side only. Nothing is tenant-configurable, because a schedule-quality threshold a tenant can lower is a Monte Carlo gate a tenant can open. THE REFUSALS ARE THE CAPABILITY: an EMPTY schedule is refused rather than scored 100 ('an empty schedule passes every defect test — no missing logic, no open ends, no long durations — and scoring it 100 would be the most dangerous number this calculation could produce, because a quality score is what gates the Monte Carlo'); a schedule below 5 activities and 2 relationships is refused against the published floor because four of the six components are statements about a NETWORK; and a score computed over fewer than four diagnosable components is refused outright rather than scaled up from what happens to be available. RULING R8, stated in the migration: the SCORE is §50's six because §50 enumerates its own composition, and the other three classes (negative float, unrealistic lags, excessive concurrency) are diagnosed and BLOCK THE GATE in their own right — without that second arm a schedule with catastrophic negative float would score in the nineties and simulate happily. `compute_case_schedule_quality` records the run (D11.29) with every blind and failing class as a refusal. Transcript: `scripts/ci-develop-slice4c-smoke.sh` steps 1 and 4. REPAIRED (20261202090300): the SCORE was correct and its STALENESS was not. `scheduleQualityFingerprint` was seven counts, and every one of the nine classes can flip without moving a count — setting `duration_hours` to 2000 on every activity took the live score from 100 to 81.3 and closed the gate while the panel kept printing '§50 Schedule Quality Score 100' with no stale label. `get_case_schedule_quality` now publishes a `classSignature` (severity, count and denominator per class), `compute_case_schedule_quality` records it, and both sides compare one definition of 'the diagnosis changed'. The `unrealistic_lags` numerator also counted dependencies whose endpoints were not both present as activities while its denominator did not, so its share could exceed 1; same population on both sides The row's named gap was a definer write path and automatic accrual; both land, on the EXISTING substrate — `contract_performance` grown (`:49`), no `vendor_quality` table anywhere (asserted absent by the slice test). **The write path** `record_contract_performance_period` (`:183`, wired at `src/services/developService.ts:6100` → `src/components/develop/CommercialPanels.tsx:1217`) refuses before the award, refuses a period that HAS NOT FINISHED (`period_end > current_date` — reporting an open window understates every actual in it and flatters the productivity factor), refuses non-finite and negative quantities field by field at the door, and refuses a period OVERLAPPING one already recorded, naming the overlap: two rows covering the same days double every hour, every cost and every rework event the record accrues and nothing downstream could tell. A unique index on `(organization, supplier, coalesce(package,0), period_start)` holds the same rule for every writer, and `enforce_contract_performance_integrity` (`:88`) refuses a DELETE — deleting a period silently IMPROVES the record, because the rework and the incidents go with it and so do the hours they were measured against. **The accrual is a READ, and there is no column to type a score into** (asserted): `get_vendor_quality_record` (`:329`, `getVendorQualityRecord` at `developService.ts:6287`, called from the commercial panel) sums the periods and joins the supplier's deliveries, warranty claims and contract claims. **REFUSAL-FIRST, and the refusal this row turns on:** with NO period recorded it refuses entirely rather than averaging nothing — a vendor nobody has measured would otherwise report no rework, no incidents and a productivity factor of 1.00, which is the number a future procurement gets handed as evidence (spec I.15). Every derived ratio refuses SEPARATELY too: no actual hours means no productivity factor and no rework rate ('It is not 1.00'); no delivery carrying BOTH a promised and a received date means no on-time rate ('100% on time over deliveries nobody dated'); a cost total refuses across currencies AND refuses when any costed period sits on no contract, because a performance period carries no currency of its own — it inherits the contract's; **the contract-claim total is SIGNED BY DIRECTION and refuses across currencies too**, which it did not when this row was first written (`sum(settled_value)` unfiltered read a supplier who claimed 200k off the owner and had 200k of liquidated damages recovered from them identically to one who simply won 400k, and it was the one money figure in the function with no currency predicate at all — `contract_claims.direction` exists to prevent exactly that and `contract_commercial_summary` in the same slice already netted it, so the slice shipped two predicates for one quantity that disagreed); a supplier NOBODY has claimed against refuses rather than reporting a settled position of zero; and a warranty claim carrying a value with no stated currency refuses the recovery total instead of joining it, because `count(distinct currency)` ignores NULLs and a claim with no unit was silently added to the CAD ones and labelled CAD (`raise_warranty_claim` now REQUIRES a currency, and the accrual buckets a missing one because `warranty_claims` is a grown table). The four accrued quantities are finite AT THE TABLE (`contract_performance_quantities_finite`), not only at the door: the wall admits-and-records a service path, and one row of NaN made the whole record answer `answered: true` with `productivityFactor` NaN — the refusal-first rule inverted. The overlap-map ruling 13 is that `contract_packages` is the home for both the ProcurementPackage and the Contract, and this EXTENDS it — a `procurement_packages` table beside it is asserted absent by the slice test. **Every §25 field, by name:** `project_id` → `development_case_id` + `capital_project_id`; `equipment_or_scope` (refused under 20 characters — a package titled "Pumps" is not one anybody can bid, evaluate or claim against); `required_date`; `supplier_id` → `awarded_supplier_id`; and the four status dimensions below. Plus the long-lead arithmetic the blocker needs: `lead_time_days`, `forecast_delivery_date`, and `is_mandatory` with `mandatory_basis` (20 characters, enforced by CHECK for every writer — the flag is the only thing that blocks a gate, so a flag with no stated reason is one somebody sets to silence a screen). **The write path E7.02 and this row both named as missing:** `record_procurement_package` refuses a package with no stated scope, a mandatory flag with no basis, a WBS element belonging to another case, a non-planning role, and ANY edit to an AWARDED package (that is a change order, not a correction). `record_package_delivery_forecast` is the one §25 field that may move after award — the contract terms are frozen, when the equipment actually arrives is not — and it refuses a forecast on a package with no `required_date` because there is then nothing to be late against, and one on a package that has already arrived. `record_package_delivery_receipt` is THE DATED RECEIPT: it states when the equipment arrived and was inspected, refuses a future date and a date before the award, and is the ONLY thing that discharges the D6.09 slippage blockers (see that row). **`is_mandatory` is three-valued at the door:** stated true, stated false, or ABSENT. Omitting it leaves the flag exactly as it is; clearing it on a package that carries it requires `mandatory_release_basis` (20 characters) and is recorded as its own `mandatory_released` act. Every other field on the revise branch is `coalesce(stated, existing)` and this one alone was `?? false`, so a cosmetic retitle through the documented write path — which is what the shipped blank-slate form sends — cleared the flag, cleared its basis and dropped a LIVE gate blocker, with the audit row recording `is_mandatory: false` as though the author had asked for it. The scope also freezes at the OPEN act, not at the award: reading the prices and then rewriting the scope, exclusions and acceptance criteria re-decides which offer complies after the numbers are on the table. **The walls:** `enforce_procurement_package_integrity` covers INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE with the tenant arm binding every writer (a package stamped with an organization that does not own its case is refused), refuses deleting an awarded or opened package, refuses a status moved outside the door, and records the service-path writes it ADMITS through `record_procurement_service_write`; TRUNCATE revoked plus a statement guard. Money is refused at the column: `awarded_value` shipped with no constraint at all and 'NaN'::numeric was storable, which passes every `>= 0` test vacuously and turns each downstream sum into NaN. | D6.04 | Tender objects: Bidder, Bid, TechnicalEvaluation, CommercialEvaluation          | I.16     | ✅     | SEALED BID, ONE OPEN ACT, FROZEN EVALUATIONS (`20261208090100_develop_tender_sealed_bid.sql`). **Bidder** = `package_bidders`, a supplier invited to ONE package with its prequalification basis — `suppliers` stays the one supplier store. `invite_package_bidder` refuses after the envelope is open (a bidder invited then would be bidding against known prices) and NAMES a missing prequalification basis and a suspended or unassessed safety qualification instead of staying quiet. **Bid** EXTENDS `contract_bids` (`sealed_at`, `submitted_by`, `bid_ref`, `currency`, `price_basis`, withdrawal pair) — no second bid store, and `compareBids` (src/lib/supply/index.ts) keeps its rows. **THE SEAL IS ENFORCED ON THREE LAYERS, because one is not enough:** the row-level policy `cb_read` hides EVERY bid on an issued-but-unopened package from every client until that package records an open act (proven live — a signed-in member of the OWNING tenant reads 0 of 3 rows). An evaluation whose counterpart on the same bid carries the same `evaluator_id` is now refused at the door AND at the table. IMMUTABLE — no UPDATE, no DELETE. Refused before the envelope is open, refused for a withdrawn bid, refused for `ai_admin` by name (§70), refused for the bid's own submitter. **The bidder register has the same wall as its siblings:** `enforce_package_bidder_integrity` (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE plus a statement-level TRUNCATE guard) carries a tenant arm against the package's AND the supplier's organization, a marker door with `record_procurement_service_write` on the admitted service path, and refuses deleting an invitation that was answered. It shipped with ZERO triggers while every sibling had two or more: it was truncatable, service-deletable with no `security_events` row, and a row stamped with one tenant against another's package inserted cleanly and was then READ by the foreign tenant. **The tender window closes once:** `open_package_bidding` refuses a close brought FORWARD once a bid has arrived (a second call collapsed a week-long window to one second, refusing every remaining bidder as late) and records a re-issue as its own act; `withdraw_sealed_bid` refuses after the close (it contained no reference to `bids_close_at` at all, so a bid could be pulled out of a closed tender before the opening — and one bidder holds one row per package, so that bidder could never re-lodge). **Separation of duties AT THE DATABASE, in BOTH directions** because the acts can happen in either order: `enforce_bid_evaluation_integrity` refuses an evaluation by the package's awarder, and `enforce_award_separation_of_duties` (INSERT and UPDATE on `contract_packages`) refuses an award by anyone who evaluated a bid on it.
