| D6.05 | Contract object (I.16)                                                          | I.16     | ✅     | ONE CONTRACT MODEL, ON THE PACKAGE (`20261208090200_develop_contract_award.sql`) — the ruling on this row, executed: `contract_packages`' award side grown, the existing warranty_terms table kept as its warranty leg by REFERENCE (`warranty_term_id` on `contract_packages`), no `contracts` table (asserted absent by the slice test). **The award is an authority-bearing act and routes through the ONE store:** `authority_limits.action_type` gains `contract_award` (every prior action type asserted still present, because dropping one silently invalidates every adopted delegation of that kind), `sync_contract_award_authority` resolves it with the same org-node scope rule as `sync_change_authority` and the same two deliberate defaults — absence refuses and a NULL ceiling refuses (a blank ceiling is an unfinished delegation, not an unlimited one) — and a cross-currency comparison refuses rather than converting. **THE CEILING IS CUMULATIVE (4D-R8), not per contract:** it aggregates this awarder's prior awards on the same development case and refuses when the running total would cross the ceiling, because a delegation that can be defeated by splitting one procurement across two packages is not a delegation — proven live, one maintenance_manager awarded 640,000 + 640,000 + 200,000 on ONE case under a single adopted CAD 750,000 delegation, every award individually "within authority". Awards in another currency are excluded from that sum rather than converted. Not callable by ANY client role: it takes an organization argument, so a direct client call would read another tenant's adopted delegation. Slice 4D's self-adoption and stated-ceiling rules are EXTENDED to the new action type by transformation of the live bodies (`adopt_authority_limit`, `state_authority_ceiling`, `get_authority_delegations`), never by re-typing them, and each raises if its anchor has moved. **`award_contract` refuses, by name:** before the envelope is opened; over ZERO bids ('There is nothing to award' — never a count of zero evaluated bids, which reads as an evaluation that ran); with a technical OR commercial evaluation missing, naming which; on a bid an evaluation called `non_compliant`, quoting that evaluation; for an awarder who evaluated (at the door AND at the table); for the AI-operator identity (§70 — an award commits the owner's capital and what the project will legally be able to demand); and ABOVE the delegated ceiling — per contract AND cumulatively — with the escalation named and a `security_events` row, because an unauthorised attempt on the owner's capital is security-relevant. It also refuses a winning bid that states NO CURRENCY (nullable on `contract_bids`, and the ceiling's currency gate is `if p_currency is not null`, so such a bid skipped it and was compared as a bare number), locks the package row FOR UPDATE so a concurrent second award reads the sentence rather than a trigger's exception, and NAMES the live bids on the package that carry no evaluation at all — both evaluation checks are scoped to the nominated bid, so a three-bid tender could be awarded to the dearest offer with the others never assessed. **AND A DECIDED AWARD IS FROZEN FOR EVERY CALLER** (`enforce_procurement_package_integrity`, the 4D-R17 rule applied to the contract): `awarded_at`, `awarded_by`, `awarded_bid_id`, `awarded_supplier_id`, `awarded_value`, `contract_currency`, the §24 field set, `award_basis` and `award_authority_limit_id` cannot change once an award stands. That one arm closes three proven defects — two overlapping `award_contract` calls each returning a full success payload to a different supplier; a service caller rewriting `awarded_value` 640000 → 1 with the commitments still posted at 640000; and `awarded_at → NULL` re-opening the package for a second award under a different ceiling with the first award's commitments still standing. `contract_package_award_bid` holds "an award names the offer it accepts" at the SCHEMA, and the award audit row records what was actually there before instead of a hard-coded `awarded_at: null`. **The commitment feeds Slice 4's model, not a second one:** `contract_commitment_lines` names the CODED cost line (D5.29 `project_cost_items`) each line commits against, and `approve_contract_commitments` writes their sum onto `project_cost_items.commitment` through `record_cost_item`'s own door (`app.cost_item_write`), with an `audit_events` row per cost line carrying previous_state and new_state. **ONE WRITER, not just one total.** `enforce_cost_item_contract_commitment` makes that column derived for every cost line an approved contract commitment points at: an omitted value is not a clearance, and a stated disagreement is refused by name. The first version had TWO writers of one column — this slice's poster and `record_cost_item`, whose payload treats an omitted `commitment` key as NULL — so a cosmetic description edit through the Controls surface silently wiped a posted 640,000 while `contract_commitment_lines` still reported it as approved and posted, with no repair path through the product (the approval answers "already approved and posted" and the line is frozen). The claim that mattered was never about totals. `contract_commitment_position` is the ONE total: it REFUSES over zero lines (that is not a commitment of zero), REFUSES while any line carries no agreed amount and NAMES those lines (a partial sum understates the contract by exactly the amount nobody has agreed yet), and refuses a mixed-currency sum — AND refuses to compare the total to the CONTRACT VALUE across currencies, because `v_total` is in the lines' currency and `awarded_value` is in the winning bid's and nothing required them to be equal (proven live: a CAD 640,000 contract carrying one USD 640,000 commitment line reported `variance 0, overCommitted false` and was approved and posted). The approval refuses on that same predicate, so the screen and the act cannot diverge — and the screen now RENDERS the server's total rather than a JS `reduce` of its own, with `commitmentTotal` kept as a cross-check that NAMES a disagreement instead of resolving it in the client's favour. `compute_case_procurement_position` reports `committedCurrency` and refuses a case-wide total summed across currencies. Self-approval by the person who recorded the lines is refused; so is a total above the contract value (that is a change order). Full chain: the contract block of `ProcurementPanel` → `awardContract` / `recordContractCommitmentLine` / `approveContractCommitments` → RPCs → `contract_packages` + `contract_commitment_lines` + `project_cost_items` → `getPackageTender` rendered through `commitmentTotal` (as a cross-check) and `awardReadiness`, which is now passed the signed-in person's email so its separation-of-duties blocker actually fires — it was called with `awarderEvaluated: false` hard-coded, so the one blocker that matters to the person about to press Award never showed. Transcript: steps 9, 10, 12, 16 and 17. RESIDUALS, NAMED. (1) `warranty_term_id` is accepted and validated by `award_contract` but has NO selector, because the warranty_terms table still has no customer write path of its own — that is D6.06's gap and D6.06 is 🟡 for it; the award NAMES the missing warranty link rather than omitting it. (2) A contract awarded in a currency other than the case's business-case currency CANNOT be committed: a commitment line's currency is forced to its cost line's, a cost line's is inherited from the business case, and the position now refuses to compare the two across units. That is a deliberate consequence of holding no exchange rate — the refusal names both currencies and says what to do — but it means the award currency and the case currency must agree before any commitment can be posted, and nothing refuses the award itself at that point. (3) The cumulative ceiling is scoped to ONE AWARDER on ONE CASE, which is what the 4D contingency rule measures and what a delegation instrument ordinarily means by a project. Two different delegates each awarding under the same tier can still take a case above that tier's ceiling between them; aggregating across awarders would need the instrument to say whether the ceiling is personal or positional, and inventing that answer here would be a governance rule nobody stated. Commitment is Slice 6A's and is unchanged here — `project_cost_items.commitment` keeps the SINGLE WRITER `enforce_cost_item_contract_commitment` gave it, and the slice test asserts this slice writes `project_cost_items` nowhere at all. **ChangeOrder** (`contract_change_orders`, `20261209090000:63`): the award is frozen for every caller once made, so a contract moves after signature HERE and nowhere else, and `contract_current_value` (`:164`) is the ONE place the award and the approved change orders are added. `record_contract_change_order` (`:658`) refuses before the award, refuses a package outside every development case (the ceiling is measured per case, so a change order outside every case is one outside every ceiling), refuses NaN and Infinity, refuses a change that moves neither money nor time, and refuses one that would make the contract negative. `decide_contract_change_order` (`:820`) **routes through THE SAME authority evaluator the award used** — `sync_contract_award_authority`, extended BY TRANSFORMATION of its live body (raising if the anchor moved) so its CUMULATIVE 4D-R8 measure now counts this person's approved change orders as well as their awards: awarding small and changing five times was the same hole splitting a procurement across two packages was. **The measure is COMMITMENT MAGNITUDE, `sum(greatest(value_delta, 0))`, and the first draft's signed sum was not a smaller version of the ceiling but a wider hole than the one it closed** — awards attribute on `awarded_by` and change orders on `decided_by`, different sets, so a de-scope approved on a contract SOMEBODY ELSE awarded subtracted from a total it had never been added to and could take it to zero or below, where 6A's `v_committed > 0` short-circuit skips the whole arm with real history behind it. The same signed/absolute confusion ran the other way at the gate: `sync_contract_award_authority` begins `abs(p_value)`, so a CAD 650,000 REDUCTION was measured as a CAD 650,000 commitment and refused with a sentence stating the opposite of its own arithmetic. A reduction now consumes no ceiling and releases none (`greatest(value_delta, 0)` at the call as well as in the sum) and remains §70-human, role-gated, refused for its own author and pricer, refused below what is already committed or certified, and frozen once decided. **And the measure is SERIALIZED at both its doors**: `decide_contract_change_order` locks the package and then the case before it reads the value or the ceiling, and the same case lock is spliced into 6A's `award_contract` by transformation with its anchor asserted — two +40,000 change orders approved concurrently each read `alreadyCommittedOnCase` 650,000, each passed a 700,000 ceiling, and both rows recorded `contract_value_before` 650,000 against a contract standing at 730,000, so the race falsified the approval record as well as defeating the ceiling. Refused above the ceiling BY NAME with a `security_events` row, refused for the AI-operator identity (§70, at the door and at the table), refused for the person who recorded it, refused a second time behind a FOR UPDATE lock, refused for the person who last SET THE VALUE as well as the person who opened the draft (the revise branch rewrites `value_delta` and leaves `recorded_by` where it was, so one person wrote a 400,000 figure onto somebody else's 1,000 draft and approved it — `last_priced_by` moves with the number and is frozen with the rest of the record), and refused when a REDUCTION would take the contract below what is already committed **or certified** — the second half was missing and is the one that had already moved money: certification refuses to take the certified total ABOVE the contract value and nothing stopped the value being moved DOWN underneath it, so a CAD 1,800,000 contract with 1,000,000 certified and PAID was reduced to 100,000, leaving the ledger explaining a payment no contract obliges that un-paying refuses to reverse. Decided change orders are FROZEN for every writer and are never deleted. `contract_commitment_position` and `approve_contract_commitments` were transformed to read `contract_current_value`, so an approved change order can actually be committed against and both halves (`awardedValue`, `changeOrderDelta`) are reported beside the total. **Invoice** (`contract_invoices`, `20261209090100:128`): NOT PAYABLE TWICE, by FOUR walls because a duplicate payment takes four routes — a unique `(organization, supplier, lower(invoice_ref))` (the duplicate is usually the same number re-keyed against a different package, and the door names which package the first one is on); `record_invoice_payment` (`:1270`) refusing a second payment by name and quoting the date and reference; the table refusing UN-PAYING for every caller, service paths included, because clearing `paid_at` is what makes the second payment available again; and a unique payment reference among paid invoices, because one bank payment settles one invoice. `certify_contract_invoice` (`:1095`) is §70 at the door and at the table, refuses self-certification by whoever entered the invoice, refuses above the gross, and refuses when the certified total would exceed `contract_current_value` — read from the ONE `contract_invoice_position` (`:502`), which itself REFUSES over an empty invoice set ('that is neither nothing outstanding nor paid in full') and over mixed currencies. A certified invoice is frozen; a rejected one stays on the ledger. **Claim** (`contract_claims`, `:53`): FROZEN once answered — grounds, value, direction, time, the answer and the settlement — for every writer, because a claim editable after its answer leaves the answer standing against a different claim and the claim document is what a dispute is decided on. `answer_contract_claim` (`:721`) is §70, refuses the person who raised it, refuses a second answer, refuses 'accepted' at less than the amount claimed (which would make a negotiated reduction indistinguishable from a claim paid in full in every total) and refuses an answer granting more time than was claimed. **Warranty** — the pair this row called SCHEMA-ONLY now has its lifecycle (`20261209090200`). `record_warranty_term` (`:503`) REFUSES a term stating neither an end date nor a usage limit: a warranty must expire, and silently permanent cover is the failure mode. `warranty_cover_position` (`:154`) is the ONE cover predicate — every door and every screen calls it, and there is no second expiry arithmetic anywhere, which was FALSE TWICE when this row was first written: `contract_commercial_summary` counted expiry itself with `ends_on < current_date`, which put a usage-limited term past its limit in neither bucket so an exhausted warranty rendered on the case screen as a live one (it now asks the predicate once per term and RENDERS the not-assessable count); and `src/lib/develop/commercial.ts` held `warrantyCover`, a ~90-line copy of every leg of it, GATING the raise-claim button and already diverged from the server on a non-finite usage reading — deleted, with the screen now closing that control only over the one branch the server refuses for every date (a term stating neither an end nor a usage limit: two null checks, no arithmetic) and rendering the server's own `coverToday` sentence. The predicate answers `covered=false` for an expired term naming the days missed, refuses for a legacy term with no stated expiry rather than answering 'covered', and refuses the usage leg when no reading was supplied instead of assuming it. `raise_warranty_claim` (`:685`) refuses outside cover in the predicate's own words and refuses a claim already time-barred; `submit_warranty_claim` (`:825`) records TIME_BARRED with the arithmetic when the window closed while the claim sat, which is the only writer of that status; `answer_warranty_claim` (`:925`) is §70 and freezes the claim. A term is frozen once claims are admitted under it. **The read** `get_contract_commercial` (`20261209090400:139`) computes NOTHING of its own — every figure comes from the predicate that owns it — and the case screen carries the compact `contract_commercial_summary` (`:22`) spliced into `get_case_procurement` by transformation. That summary reported three things of its own and each was wrong: a confident `invoices: 0, invoicesAwaitingPayment: 0` where `contract_invoice_position` REFUSES in so many words ('that is not "nothing outstanding" and it is not "paid in full"'), so two surfaces of one slice answered one question oppositely and the refusal-first one was the one the planner did not see (it now carries the position's refusal verbatim and reports NULL, not zero); `claimsOpen` alone, which rendered 'nobody has claimed' and 'every claim has been answered' as the same '0 open claim(s)' (`claimsRaised` is beside it now); and `settlementNotCarried`, a difference between the net settled claims and EVERY approved change order — nothing links a claim to the change order that carries it and the delta is mostly scope, so the figure was wrong in both directions, a false all-clear on agreed money when an unrelated change order happened to match and an invented shortfall when a scope change sat beside a settlement. The SENTENCE stays and the arithmetic is gone: a number nobody can derive is worse than none. **Surface:** `/develop` → `DevelopmentCaseWorkspacePage.tsx:2959` → `ProcurementPanels.tsx:1343` → `src/components/develop/CommercialPanels.tsx` (record and decide a change order, receive/certify/pay an invoice, raise and answer a claim, record a warranty term and claim under it, record a performance period, link a specification). | D6.09 | ProcurementPackage §25 (four status dimensions + gate blocking)                 | III.§25  | ✅     | FOUR DIMENSIONS, AND A BLOCK THAT IS CONSEQUENTIAL (`20261208090000_develop_procurement_package.sql`). `sync_procurement_status_dimensions` names §25's four verbatim and `sync_procurement_status_values` gives each its own vocabulary; the CHECK on `contract_packages` READS those functions rather than repeating the list, `PROCUREMENT_STATUS_VALUES` (src/lib/develop/procurement.ts) mirrors them and the slice test pins the two together, so a fifth value cannot appear on one side only. All four exist from birth and `get_case_procurement` returns all four on every package — a package shown with three reads as complete on the one nobody tracked. `set_procurement_package_status` moves ONE dimension with a stated basis and an audit row carrying previous_state and new_state, and refuses `commercial = awarded` BY NAME because only `award_contract` writes that value — typed by hand it would be an award nobody made, and the dimension is what the screens read. **It refuses moving OFF it too.** The guard was one-directional, so a planner set the commercial dimension of a package holding a live award to `cancelled` — leaving `awarded_at`, the supplier, the value and the whole §24 set standing while every screen rendered the contract as cancelled — and it could not be undone, because typing `awarded` back is refused and `award_contract` refuses a second award. It also refuses `commercial = cancelled` on a MANDATORY package by name: leg 1 does not stop firing because somebody typed `cancelled`, so a cancelled mandatory package blocked every gate on the case for ever with the wall's own stated remedy (award it) no longer possible. Releasing the mandatory flag is the act, and it costs a twenty-character judgement. And `delivery = received_and_inspected` is refused by name — see below. **THE GATE BLOCKING RIDES THE ONE PREDICATE.** `case_procurement_gate_obligations` returns THREE types in the shape Slice 3C's `case_gate_outstanding_obligations` speaks, and is APPENDED into it by the same transformation idiom Slices 5B and 5D used — the migration RAISES rather than proceeding if the anchor has moved, and building a second gate evaluator is refused in the file's own words. `enforce_gate_review_outstanding_obligations` gains all three types AND a refusal message that describes what it now checks (a wall whose message no longer matches is worse than no message, so the transformation fails rather than widening the type list alone). ONE predicate, four consumers: the readiness screen (`get_gate_readiness`), the gate-review RPC, the persistence wall, and `get_case_procurement`. **PROVEN IN THE TRANSCRIPT** (step 3): a mandatory long-lead package whose award-by date has passed refuses `record_case_gate_review` AND refuses a direct `stage_gate_reviews` insert by a writer with RLS switched off; step 10 shows the same write going through once the contract is awarded; step 11 shows the second type — mandatory long-lead SLIPPAGE, this row's own words — blocking the same gate off a recorded forecast, and clearing only when a DATED RECEIPT records that the equipment arrived; step 17 shows the third. **THE RULE IS DECLARED, NOT INFERRED:** both legs require the human-stated `is_mandatory` flag with its basis AND the dates to compute with. A mandatory package missing `required_date` or `lead_time_days` is absent from the blocker list and NAMED as not assessable by `get_case_procurement` — an alarm wired to a date nobody recorded is worse than no alarm — and the empty package set REFUSES rather than reporting zero packages late. **THE THIRD LEG, AND WHY THE FIRST TWO WERE NOT ENOUGH.** Leg 1 (`procurement_package_unawarded`) stops the moment anything is awarded and never asks whether the award happened before the award-by date; leg 2 (`procurement_package_late`) needs a `forecast_delivery_date`, and recording one is entirely voluntary. So the exact state this row exists for — MANDATORY, awarded sixty days late, no forecast recorded, contract completing 170 days after the project needs the equipment — produced ZERO blockers and the gate passed. Leg 3 (`procurement_package_contract_late`) reads evidence that is always present, because §24 makes `contract_completion_date` mandatory on every awarded package: a contract that completes after the date the project needs the thing cannot deliver on time BY ITS OWN TERMS. And a mandatory awarded package that states neither a forecast nor a completion date is reported NOT ASSESSABLE by name (`deliveryAssessable` / `mandatoryDeliveryNotAssessable`), never counted as on time. **Lateness is read off the DATES, and DISCHARGED off a DATE.** Both halves matter and the second one was wrong: the discharge term was `delivery_status <> 'received_and_inspected'`, which one planner could type through `set_procurement_package_status` with a ten-character basis — proven live, the blocker went from firing to silent while the recorded dates still said the equipment was 45 days late, and the gate review the wall had just refused was then accepted with nothing arrived. The column's own comment forbade exactly that. All three legs now discharge on `actual_delivery_date`, written by `record_package_delivery_receipt`, which refuses a future date and a date before the award; `contract_package_receipt_pair` holds the date and the status together for every writer, and `set_procurement_package_status` refuses that status value by name and points at the act. Lineage: `compute_case_procurement_position` records a `calculation_runs` row under `case_procurement_position` INCLUDING when the report refused and carrying every per-contract commitment refusal by package code. Surface: the blocker list on `ProcurementPanel` — rendered from the server's rows and the server's own arithmetic, with no client re-derivation — plus `procurement_package_unawarded` / `procurement_package_late` / `procurement_package_contract_late` rendered by name on the readiness screen (src/components/develop/ReadinessPanels.tsx), and the delivery-receipt control on the package (without it the discharge would be unreachable from the product). Transcript: steps 2, 3, 10, 11, 13, 16 and 17. The read REPORTS the linked WBS element's minimum imported float as evidence and says plainly when the schedule carries none; the blocker fires on the declared mandatory flag. DECLARED rows stay clearable, because a person's answer is their only discharge path. | D7.08 | Forward constraint-free work metric                                      | I.28       | ✅     | ONE CALCULATION WITH D7.20, and this row and that one cite the same symbol — the specification names the same quantity twice (I.28 'forward constraint-free work', III.§49 'Constraint-Free Work Index') and building two would put two answers behind one question. `get_constraint_free_work_index` (20261212090300:162) produces BOTH faces from one payload over one denominator: the index today, and the FORWARD figure adding packages whose burn-down forecasts them clear before they are needed. | D11.06 | Authoritative-version resolution per thread object                                                                       | II.2           | ✅     | Built (Slice 5C, `20261206090100_develop_thread_authoritative_version.sql`). Exactly one authoritative revision per object, held by the partial unique index `idx_thread_version_one_authoritative` — an index, not a trigger that counts rows, because two concurrent releases both counting zero incumbents both succeed. Supersession is RECORDED, never overwritten: the incumbent moves to `superseded` and both pointers are written, and a superseded revision with no successor is refused by a CHECK. Recording a revision (`record_thread_version`) is deliberately separate from releasing it (`declare_thread_version_authoritative`), and §70 bars the AI-operator identity from the release at the door AND at the wall (`enforce_frontline_judgement_is_human` bound to `declared_by`, INSERT and UPDATE). `enforce_thread_version_integrity` refuses un-superseding, un-releasing, re-labelling and a status moved outside the recorded act, for every writer. A released row is immutable in what it SAYS as well as what it is: `content_ref`, `issued_on`, `change_summary` and `declaration_basis` are frozen once the row leaves `draft`, so "Rev C is authoritative" cannot come to point at a document nobody released. A RETIRED object resolves to NO current revision — retirement never touches the version rows, so the incumbent would otherwise read as current for ever; the refusal still names the label so the history is not lost, and `check_thread_continuity` reports the same state as a gap. Reachable: `resolve_thread_authoritative_version` / `record_thread_version` / `declare_thread_version_authoritative` → `resolveThreadAuthoritativeVersion` / `recordThreadVersion` / `declareThreadVersionAuthoritative` (src/services/developService.ts) → `readAuthoritativeVersion` (`src/lib/develop/thread.ts`) → `VersionPanel` in `DigitalThreadPanel`, where the revision to release is chosen from the DRAFT IDS `get_case_thread_graph` emits per object — a count cannot be released, and with only a count the release act would have been reachable from psql and from nowhere in the product. | D11.07 | Downstream-impact and change-receipt tracking                                                                            | II.2           | ✅     | Built (Slice 5C, `20261206090300_develop_thread_impact_receipts.sql`), extending the MOC/`propagate_risk_objective_change` precedent this row cited: `raise_thread_change_receipts` fires ON the change (an AFTER trigger on the version becoming authoritative AND superseding), never from a report, and writes one `thread_change_receipts` row per live downstream object at `unacknowledged` — an explicit state, not an absence. A FIRST issue raises none. `acknowledge_thread_receipt` demands a note on BOTH terminal readings and keeps `not_applicable` distinct from `acknowledged`; §70 bars a machine and §42 bars the person who declared the revision, at the door and at the wall (`enforce_thread_receipt_integrity`). `get_case_thread_impact` REFUSES rather than under-reporting: an object with no live hop is named as unassessed instead of `0 downstream impacts`, and a traversal whose region contains a chain skip, an unreleased object or the depth limit returns the reached set as a stated FLOOR with a NULL count. The traversal also refuses on what it cannot SEE: a severed hop out of the region, a live hop into a retired object and a backward hop are each named as gaps, because the walk reads only live links and a severance is exactly the event that removes something from the affected set while leaving it physically downstream. Every receipt records whether the region it was raised over was GAPPED, so a case whose receipts are all answered cannot read as "the change landed everywhere" when the sibling read refuses to call that region complete; and zero receipts beside a non-zero supersession count REFUSES rather than reporting "no revision has superseded another". The receipt wall resolves both endpoints and the source revision on INSERT as well as UPDATE, and §42 covers the INSERT — a receipt can be born answered, and the declarer cannot sign that one either. Reachable: `getCaseThreadImpact` / `getCaseThreadReceipts` / `acknowledgeThreadReceipt` → `readThreadImpact` / `readThreadReceipts` → `DigitalThreadPanel`, whose acknowledgement note is keyed per receipt. | D11.20 | Digital thread continuity invariant ('must never break')                                                                 | III.§26        | ✅     | Built and ENFORCED AT THE DATABASE (Slice 5C, `20261206090200_develop_thread_continuity.sql` + the walls in `20261206090000`), not reported by a job. `break` is defined in the migration header as exactly four routes and each is enforced: anchor loss (NOT NULL + in-tenant + `enforce_asset_thread_anchor`), dangling link (`enforce_thread_link_integrity`), silent severance (DELETE refused on all five tables for every caller, TRUNCATE revoked with statement guards, endpoints/kind/case immutable, status columns movable only through the recorded acts) and version-chain hole (partial unique index + CHECK). Where a break MUST be permitted it is recorded, never quiet: `sever_thread_link`, `retire_thread_object` (which severs every live hop in the same transaction and counts them) and `reanchor_thread_object` each write `record_thread_severance`, as do the case, asset and canonical-row cascades; the organization cascade is the one route that records nothing and the header says so. RECORDED ALSO MEANS READABLE: the asset cascade stamps each affected case's real id (a null case matches no read, which for the person looking afterwards is the same as silent), and `get_org_thread_severances` is the tenant-scoped read the CASE cascade survives into — the case-scoped one refuses on the very case those rows record the loss of. The ledger itself has a door: `record_thread_severance` is revoked from `service_role` too and sets a transaction-local marker the INSERT wall demands, so a forged row naming a real engineer cannot slip in and then be made permanent by the append-only guard. Attribution comes from the ROUTE, never from whether an actor column is filled — both cascades record whoever held the session. §70 bars a machine from all three human acts at the door and at the wall, and all three now write `security_events`. `check_thread_continuity` REPORTS the residual the walls cannot pre-empt and separates BREAKS from GAPS — `intact` is about breaks only and is NULL while refused — and it uses the CLOSED org gate rather than the repo's wider service-read convention, because it returns break details naming objects. Reachable: `checkThreadContinuity` / `severThreadLink` / `retireThreadObject` / `getCaseThreadSeverances` / `getOrgThreadSeverances` → `readThreadContinuity` / `readThreadSeverances` / `readOrgThreadSeverances` (`src/lib/develop/thread.ts`) → `DigitalThreadPanel`, where the hop to sever is chosen from the live hops rather than typed as a bare id. The canonical-row cascade is reachable only through the canonical PARENT, and that is a fact about the product rather than a convenience: slice 5A refuses a design_requirements DELETE by name — a requirement is WAIVED, never deleted — so the act that reaches this route is deleting the capital_projects row whose design_requirements and acceptance_tests the thread objects ARE, and the transcript drives it that way and asserts the 5A refusal beside it, on the same row, before the cascade takes it. | D11.26 | Event bus with five named events                                                                                         | III.§71-78     | ✅     | Built (Slice 5D, `20261207090000_develop_event_bus.sql`). All FIVE §71-78 events exist by name — `sync_develop_event_names()` holds GateRequirementChanged, RiskThresholdExceeded, ScheduleUpdated, WorkPackageBlocked, CommissioningTestFailed verbatim and the table's CHECK reads that array — and each is emitted by an AFTER trigger on the table whose change IS the event, per the register's own mechanism ruling (triggers, not Kafka): stage_gate_criteria, risk_indicator_observations, shutdown_tasks, work_orders, acceptance_tests. Case scope arrives through the CANONICAL joins only (gate→framework→case, indicator→risk→case, activity→WBS→case, asset→development_case_assets, project→capital_project_id); an act touching no case emits nothing and the smoke proves that boundary in BOTH directions. RiskThresholdExceeded is a CROSSING, not a level: it compares the observation with the previous one, so a run of criticals emits once. One event per act per case per transaction, enforced by a unique index on (case, dedupe key, txid) rather than a check-then-insert — a two-activity batch is one ScheduleUpdated. **AN EMITTER WITH NO SUBSCRIBER WOULD BE THEATRE, so there is one and it ACTS:** `dispatch_develop_event` runs synchronously inside the emitting transaction, applies the rules-as-data set (`sync_develop_event_rules()`) — reading the observed state for RiskThresholdExceeded (critical blocks, warning asks) and the case's OWN review history for GateRequirementChanged (a criterion edited under a recorded decision blocks; one authored during framework setup does not) — and writes one delivery per event, asserted 1:1 by the transcript. THE CONSEQUENCE IS ENFORCED, not displayed: `case_event_consequence_obligations` is appended to case_gate_outstanding_obligations and REFUSED OVER by enforce_gate_review_outstanding_obligations (both wired BY TRANSFORMATION of the live bodies, raising if the anchor moved — the 5B idiom), so a gate review cannot be recorded while a blocking consequence stands, for every writer including a marker-holding service caller. A gate-level consequence blocks its own gate only (ruling 5D-R18 — found by running the sibling transcripts, which the over-broad first draft broke). §70/§42 on the answer: `answer_develop_event_consequence` refuses ai_admin BY NAME and the wall refuses it for every writer on `answered_by` (INSERT and UPDATE), the person whose act emitted a blocking event cannot answer it, a note under 20 characters is refused, a second answer is refused, and a marker-holding caller still cannot downgrade `blocking` to `attention`. NOT A THIRD AUDIT LEDGER (justified in the migration header): the event body is append-only and carries the row identity and classification, never a second account of the decision, and `emit_develop_event` still writes the audit_events row with previous_state/new_state — one audit row per event, asserted. An empty list is a SENTENCE naming the five acts and the window, never "0 events". Full chain: Case Workspace event-bus section (`DevelopEventBusPanel` in src/components/develop/EventBusPanels.tsx, mounted in DevelopmentCaseWorkspacePage) → `getCaseDevelopEvents` / `answerDevelopEventConsequence` / `getCaseEventGateBlockers` → `get_case_develop_events` / `answer_develop_event_consequence` / `case_event_consequence_obligations` → rows under RLS → outstanding and answered consequences on screen with `readDevelopEvents` / `answerBlockedReason` (`src/lib/develop/events.ts`, 15 unit tests). The gate-blocking list on the panel is read from the WALL'S OWN predicate rather than re-filtered on the client — enforced truth and displayed truth are the same rows or they are two answers. REPAIRED UNDER ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, six defects, each reproduced live before it was closed and each now covered by a migration-contract test that fails without the fix (the slice-5D entry in src/test, added because every sibling slice ships one and 5D did not — which is why all six got past the transcript): (1) `case_event_consequence_obligations` was SECURITY DEFINER, granted to `authenticated`, and filtered on the CASE ALONE — a member of any tenant could read another tenant's blocking obligations, verbatim criterion text included, by uuid; it now carries its parent's exact org guard, and admits the uid-less trigger/service caller so the wall is not switched off. (2) `emit_develop_event` and `dispatch_develop_event` were still executable by `service_role` — Supabase's default privileges grant it and only three of four roles were revoked — and `emit_develop_event` is the ONLY door into an append-only ledger, so one POST from any edge function manufactured a permanent gate blocker naming a source row that does not exist; both are now revoked from every client role. (3) The org and the case had to AGREE and did not: a mismatched pair was read AND answered by a foreign tenant; enforced at the wall now (5D-R20). (4) The collapse key was `(case, dedupe_key, txid)`, so a CRITICAL crossing arriving after a WARNING in one transaction was discarded by `do nothing` — the indicator was critical, the bus said warning, no gate blocked, and no audit row either; the key now carries the CONSEQUENCE CLASS from `sync_develop_event_consequence()`, THE one classifier both the emitter and the consumer read, and dispatch RAISES if the two ever disagree (5D-R19). A batch of one class is still one event. (5) `RiskThresholdExceeded` was INSERT-only on a table with no append-only guard, and `ScheduleUpdated` did not cover DELETE; both now cover the act. `WorkPackageBlocked` suppressed a re-emit on a row whose first pass emitted nothing, so create-then-link missed the event entirely. (6) The panel called the predicate WITHOUT a gate and printed "a gate review recorded while they stand is refused at the database" — false for every gate but one, proven by a `proceed` that went through the wall; it now states, per row, whether the consequence blocks every gate or one named gate. The model's answer is validated by the deterministic half (`parseFrameworkProposal`, supabase/functions/_shared/develop-agent-core.ts, 34 vitest cases): a non-canonical stage key is REFUSED, not mapped (mapping 'FEL-2' onto a lifecycle key would be a silent guess inside a governance model); orphan gates and requirements are dropped and REPORTED; is_mandatory stays false unless the model says true; an empty answer is a refusal, not an empty framework. "stigg/fast"` three lines under a comment saying no model id was hardcoded, and the test only forbade inline literals — the sentence asserted more than either delivered. CANNOT APPROVE, and not as a promise: the boundary is four shipped refusals it composes with — `record_case_gate_review` refuses ai_admin by name, `enforce_gate_review_provenance` refuses a client writing an outcome directly, `enforce_gate_review_recorder_is_human` refuses a review attributed to that identity for EVERY writer, and `gate_review_sod_position` reports the same to the screen. The agent holds no path to any of those tables. Its only write is `record_gate_agent_report` (20261123090200), and the report's readiness, blockers and blocked verdict are read INSIDE the RPC from the evaluator rather than supplied by the caller — a model cannot report a number it invented. `gate_agent_reports` has no outcome, decision, approval or verdict column (asserted by name in developSlice3dMigration.test.ts and again live against information_schema in the transcript), pins `advisory` true with a CHECK, is immutable on UPDATE, and COUNTS the open-risk family without naming it because a report row is org-readable and the risk ladder is not. Negative test: transcript step 4 plus step 2's four §70 doors. **REPAIR PASS 2026-08-28 (adversarial review).** Two defects: (1) `record_gate_agent_report`'s entire authorisation was "has a profile", so the lowest-privileged member could author an immutable, undeletable, org-readable row carrying an agent key, a model and a narrative, rendered under a bot icon as the agent's reading — now gated to the same role set every sibling RPC in the slice uses, with an unbounded `narrative` bounded at 6000 by a CHECK and a named refusal. (2) The redaction was of the risk's NAME only. This DEFINER function calls the INVOKER evaluator, so readiness came back with definer rights, and existence + count + a persisted `blocker_count` are exactly what the ladder withholds — a technician could use the RPC as an oracle for restricted risks. | D12.09 | Requirements Agent (missing/unverified/orphan/inconsistent)                    | III.§59  | ✅     | Built 2026-08-31 (Slice 5A), repaired the same day. `develop-requirements-agent` (supabase/functions/develop-requirements-agent/index.ts, inside the approved deploy boundary) reports §59's four families plus unowned and, after the repair, outside-the-§10-taxonomy. **THE DETERMINISTIC HALF IS DETERMINISTIC.** `get_case_requirement_findings` computes missing verification method, unverified (split three ways — nobody looked / looked and failed / the date passed), orphan (no objective, plus absent-from-WBS DELEGATED to `get_case_scope_traceability` and REFUSED rather than reported as zero), SIX deterministic inconsistency classes and unowned — every finding carrying its record link. Two of the six are the repair: `verified_over_an_unretracted_failure` and `passed_without_superseding_the_failure`, both `blocking`, because a recorded FAILURE superseded by a later pass raised nothing at all and every derived number read clean. The sixth family, `outside_spec10_taxonomy`, is the other repair: ruling 2's whole justification for keeping the five legacy categories is that such a requirement is REPORTED, and nothing reported it. **PROPOSES ONLY — now true at every door, and proven at the DATABASE.** The claim was overstated: `link_requirement_thread` admitted `ai_admin`, and one call over the product API with a real AI-operator token took a requirement from 4 findings to 2 (`unowned` and `orphan/no_objective` both vanished, `audit_events.actor = 'ai_admin'`); `record_case_requirement` accepted a `verification_method` from the same identity, which is the act ruling 4 refuses at `create_requirement_verification` for exactly this reason. Both are now refused BY NAME. The identity may still RECORD a requirement — that ADDS findings — and may not state its method, its owner, its objective, its acceptance criteria, its KPI or its parent. Smoke step 8d measures the reach: findingCount before = findingCount after, and zero `requirement_thread` audit rows with actor `ai_admin`. `requirement_agent_reports` has NO column that can hold a status, result, outcome, approval, decision or verdict, `advisory` is pinned by a CHECK, and every count is read INSIDE the RPC from the finding engine. **THE MODEL'S HALF NOW REACHES THE SCREEN.** It did not: `findings` came only from the SQL engine, which writes `source = 'deterministic'` on every row, so the AI-generated badge, the "capped at attention" disclaimer and `orderedFindings`' AI-below-facts sort were all unreachable, and a successful run produced no visible change on the page. `aiFindingsAsFindings` merges them (labelled from a TypeScript literal as the RPC labels from a SQL literal), `agentModelNote` states that a model was asked and returned NOTHING rather than rendering silence, and `aiDropped` is surfaced. `parseRequirementInconsistencies` DROPS a reference the case does not carry rather than matching it to the nearest one; the RPC drops-and-REPORTS the same. **PROMPT INJECTION AND BOUNDS (repair).** Requirement statements are customer-authored free text and were interpolated raw; they are now fenced in an explicit untrusted-data delimiter that the system prompt names, with line breaks and role markers neutralised and each statement bounded — nothing deleted, only the structure that made a statement read as prompt. The stored narrative carries an explicit `AI-GENERATED` marker between the deterministic reading and the model's prose, which were previously joined by a blank line into one paragraph on an immutable, undeletable, org-readable row. `p_model` is capped at 200 characters at the RPC and by a CHECK, and the caller-supplied findings array is capped at 50 with the excess DROPPED AND REPORTED — one planner call had stored a 200,000-character model name and 5,054 findings. The RPC returns the `byFamily` it STORED, so the families sum to the count it returns. Model-agnostic: no vendor name and no model id in the agent's source. Refusal-first: over an empty requirement set the engine refuses, the RPC records NO row at all, and the edge function returns the refusal without calling a model. Reports are on demand, not scheduled. Immutable, undeletable, not truncatable, org-scoped, role-gated, bounded at the database. UI: the Requirements Agent card on the Case Workspace, with `readRequirementFindings` and `findingsHeadline` stating a refusal as a refusal and never as "0 findings". THE REMAINING GAP, stated rather than implied: (a) NO RBD is computed and the refusal says why — nothing in this repository stores a redundancy structure for a case's assets, and assuming series would produce a system reliability with an invented model behind it (`evaluateRbd` stays uncalled on purpose); (b) FMEA, PM strategy and reliability-growth remain org/asset-scoped on the existing agent surfaces (ReliabilityPage/ModellingStudio, reliability-engineer-core) and are NOT case-scoped by this slice; (c) the case-scoped reading is deterministic — no model narrates it, and the report's `model` column stays null. The profile must now TIE TO THE SCOPE the server just re-read: every `targetId` and `assetId` it names must be one this database put in scope and it must cover all of them, refused rather than trimmed. | D13.06 | Assurance Case screen (claim → evidence → confidence)                     | III.§44  | ✅     | Built 2026-08-28 (Slice 3D). `get_case_assurance_case` (20261123090400) composes §44's five parts for one case: CLAIMS (`assurance_case_claims` — the sentence, its type, its owner, and a human position with a stated basis), EVIDENCE (`assurance_claim_evidence` — a RECORDED link with the basis on which this evidence bears on this claim, and `bearing` supports/qualifies/CONTRADICTS, because an assurance case that can only hold supporting evidence is a marketing document), CONFIDENCE (the D11.22 §46 composite per item via `compute_evidence_confidence`, no second arithmetic), ASSUMPTIONS (`risk_assumptions` scoped to the case — the ONE assumption store, ruling 5, no new table) and INDEPENDENT REVIEW (`get_case_assurance_position`, carrying competency, conflicts and rank from Slice 3C), plus open issues from the shipped risk, condition and commitment stores. SECURITY INVOKER, so the risk-sensitivity ladder applies to the risks it names. THE DESIGN DECISION: the claim→evidence link is recorded, never inferred. Joining claims to evidence on word overlap would look complete on day one and put a reviewer's name on a link nobody made, so a claim with nothing linked renders the server's own sentence — 'Nothing supports it and nothing contradicts it — it is an assertion' — which is the row that gets work done. NO AGGREGATE IS INVENTED: the screen reports the highest and lowest supporting confidence and how many items the computation refused, and deliberately no single number (combining independent evidence needs an independence assumption this product has not stated; '0.71' would be believed). Asserted both statically and live. §70 and fail-closed: `set_assurance_claim_position` refuses the AI-operator identity by name, refuses 'supported' on a claim with nothing linked — at the RPC AND at the persistence boundary — and `unlink_assurance_claim_evidence` refuses pulling the last support out from under a supported claim; evidence from another case cannot be borrowed in. Write paths: `record_assurance_claim`, `link_assurance_claim_evidence`, `unlink_assurance_claim_evidence`, `set_assurance_claim_position`. UI: /develop/cases/:caseId/assurance (`AssuranceCasePage`, routed in App.tsx and linked from the Case Workspace header). Transcript: ci-develop-slice3d-smoke.sh step 6. **REPAIR PASS 2026-08-28 (adversarial review).** Three defects: (1) the "none scored" confidence sentence formatted with EVERY link while calling them "supporting item(s)", so a claim with three CONTRADICTING links and nothing supporting it was described to the reviewer as having three supporting items — on the one screen whose header promises contradicting evidence is first-class. It counts supporting links now and emits a distinct sentence for the contradicted-only case (smoke 8i). (2) `link_assurance_claim_evidence` is DEFINER and never consulted `evidence_items_risk_sensitive`, while the read is INVOKER and does — so a link to evidence the linker could not read produced a claim rendering `"position":"supported"` and "it is an assertion" simultaneously. The link now applies `can_read_risk`, and the read reports `withheldCount` via `assurance_claim_link_total` instead of silently rendering short. (3) `owner_id`/`success_outcome_id`/`requirement_id` were bare casts in the DECLARE block, so an unparseable value raised a raw 22P02 before any validation could name the field; they go through `sync_text_as_*` with named refusals.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

| D13.08 | Integrated Controls screen (six control dimensions, one view)             | III.§44  | ✅     | `get_case_integrated_controls` (20261203090300) serves spec §44's "scope, schedule, cost, risk, change, procurement in one coherent view" and the Case Workspace renders it (`ChangeAndControlsPanel`). THE SCREEN COMPOSES RECORDED RUNS AND COMPUTES NOTHING: each dimension is the LATEST `calculation_runs` row for its key (`case_scope_growth`, `case_schedule_quality`, `case_earned_value`, `case_risk_schedule_economics`, `case_change_control`, `case_contingency_consumption`) read through `sync_latest_calculation_run`, and the migration test asserts the read calls no live `get_case_*` for a figure and never calls `record_calculation_run` — a screen that recomputed would be a second source of truth, and the smoke proves the run count is unchanged after loading it. There are no blank tiles: a dimension with no run says NO RUN RECORDED and names the compute function, a dimension whose last run REFUSED says so and lists its reasons, and the LIVE READ IS DELIBERATELY NOT A FALLBACK (a figure from it would be a number with no lineage under a lineage caption — the 4A failure). PROCUREMENT is rendered EMPTY AND NAMED as the seventh tile because no procurement calculation exists in Sync Develop yet: a five-tile "integrated controls" view would quietly redefine what integrated means and a reader could not tell missing from clean. THE CROSS-TENANT HOLE THIS SCREEN OPENED IS CLOSED: `sync_latest_calculation_run` shipped SECURITY DEFINER, granted to `authenticated`, taking an arbitrary case uuid and never calling `app_current_org()` — PostgREST exposed it directly, so any signed-in identity, including one with no `user_profiles` row for which every other 4D RPC returns `forbidden`, could read the full recorded payload of every calculation in the product for any case: another tenant's contingency totals and ledger ids, their earned-value suite, their decision-debt figure with the decision question quoted verbatim in the refusal, and the email of whoever computed it. The canonical sibling `get_case_calculation_lineage` carries that gate; the two other internal helpers with this shape were revoked from `authenticated` in this same slice and this one was missed because the definer-tenancy scan keys on argument NAMES matching org/organization/tenant and this takes `p_case_id`. It now resolves the caller's organization INSIDE the function AND is revoked from every client role, and the smoke probes it as a foreign tenant. STALENESS IS BY CONTENT, AND THE SCREEN SAYS WHAT IT CHECKED: every tile used to print `codeVersion · date` unconditionally with no staleness path at all — an earned-value run from before three cost re-baselines rendered identically to a fresh one, and the contingency tile printed a clean caption directly above a section reading "the ledger has moved since this run was recorded". The read now returns the digests for the four dimensions whose fingerprint it can reproduce WITHOUT running their kernel (contingency, change, and both decision calculations), and each of those tiles is marked stale with its code-version caption suppressed when the fingerprint has moved. RESIDUAL, NAMED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: for scope, schedule, cost and risk the kernel's fingerprint (`basisDigest`, the traceability broken-link count, the policy digests) cannot be produced here without performing that kernel's own read — the one thing this screen must not do — so those tiles carry `stalenessCheckable: false` and a caption that SAYS the currency of the figure was not checked here, pointing at the panel where the live read and the recorded run sit side by side. An unchecked caption and a checked one must not look the same. THE TILES SHOW THE FIELDS THE DIMENSION IS ABOUT: `Object.entries(outputs).slice(0, 5)` was an arbitrary truncation (jsonb orders keys by length then bytewise) that rendered the cost tile as `ac, es, ev, pv, bac` and silently dropped `cpi`, `spi`, `eac`, `vac` — the entire earned-value suite D5.05/D5.06 names — along with `currency`, so the money carried no unit. `DIMENSION_HEADLINE_FIELDS` names the set per dimension and the tile COUNTS whatever it does not show. Transcript: slice-4d smoke steps 11 and 14. |
| D13.09 | Execution Readiness screen (work-package board)                           | III.§44  | ✅     | Two live readiness surfaces already existed — RecoveryControlCenter (readiness refresh + constraint declarations + start/complete) and SchedulerPanel (feasibility + hard/soft release verdicts) (src/components/RecoveryControlCenter.tsx:240-262; src/components/SchedulerPanel.tsx:243,300) — and the per-package board was the gap. Slice 7B builds it on the one engine (RULING 22): `get_execution_readiness_board` (20261211090100) returns every unreleased work package × the ONE release verdict × the hard constraints still open × their owners (role and email) × the last recorded field-readiness assessment, org-wide or case-scoped. It COMPOSES rather than recomputes — the verdict is `sync_work_package_release_verdict` verbatim (including its seventh state `stale`, worn in RED with the server's own itemized gaps under it, and with the 'assessed on …' note kept in its amber register rather than dropped to quiet grey the moment `assessed` is true), the blocking items are read from `restoration_constraints`, and the assessment is the `calculation_runs` row read back as it was written — a REFUSED run counts as not assessed, never as reassurance. Refusal-first: an organization with no packages gets a refusal sentence by name, because an empty board reads as 'nothing is waiting on anybody'. Undated packages sort LAST, since a null required-by is 'nobody said when' and at the top of a work-down list it would read as most urgent. A package nobody has assessed says so in its own row, in amber, rather than as a blank. Reachable: src/App.tsx route /execution-readiness → src/pages/ExecutionReadinessPage.tsx → `getExecutionReadinessBoard` in src/services/developService.ts, linked from src/pages/DevelopmentCaseWorkspacePage.tsx.
